At AIB, our values guide how we work and how we support each other. We’re looking for someone who puts  Customer First , takes initiative and  Owns the Outcome , and is always looking for ways to  Eliminate Complexity . You’ll treat colleagues and customers with fairness and  Show Respect , and you’ll thrive in a culture built on collaboration where we  Be One Team  to deliver meaningful impact.
Location/Office Policy: Central Park, Leopardstown, Dublin 18 (3 days per week in office)
Are you interested in building a career in AML / Financial Crime within a supportive and fast‑paced environment?
Do you enjoy analytical work, learning from experienced colleagues, and contributing to the effective management of financial crime risk?
What is the Role:
The Correspondent Banking AML (CB AML) Team supports the management of AML risk across AIB’s global correspondent banking network. This role supports the completion of KYC reviews, analysis of payments and transaction data, and responses to AML‑related queries, under guidance from senior team members.
This is a collaborative role within an experienced AML team, offering strong exposure to correspondent banking, international payments, and AML risk management.
Key accountabilities:
As part of the Correspondent Banking AML Team, you will:
Support the completion of KYC / AML reviews for bank and financial institution counterparties
Assist with analysing transaction and payments data and contribute to written assessments
Support the management of internal and external AML‑related queries, escalating issues as required
Work closely with team members and stakeholders across the Bank
Manage assigned tasks effectively, demonstrating reliability and attention to detail
What you will bring:
2 years’ experience in banking, financial services, or a relevant regulatory / compliance environment
An interest in KYC / AML and financial crime risk management
Strong attention to detail with good written and analytical skills
Ability to work effectively in a structured, fast‑paced environment
Good communication skills and a willingness to learn and ask questions
A collaborative team player with a positive and engaged approach
Basic understanding of AML regulation or a willingness to develop this knowledge
Third‑level qualification required
Competent   MS Excel skills (e.g. basic formulas, data handling); advanced skills an advantage
Exposure to data tools or reporting (e.g. Power BI, Tableau) is beneficial but not essential
A Reminder of What We Offer:
We are committed to offering our colleagues choice and flexibility in how we work and live and our hybrid working model enables our people to balance their time between working from home and their designated office, subject to their role, the needs of our customers and business requirements.
Some of our benefits include;
Market leading Pension Scheme
Healthcare Scheme
Variable Pay
Employee Assistance Programme
Family leave options
Two volunteer days per year
Please click  here   for further information about AIB’s PACT – Our Commitment to You.
Key Capabilities
Behavioural Capabilities
Ensures accountability:  takes ownership of work, commitments and outputs, ensuring tasks are completed accurately, on time and in line with agreed expectations.
Collaboration:  Works effectively with colleagues and contributes positively to team outcomes
Customer First:  considers customer impact when escalating issues and supports solutions that minimise disruption to customer.  Learns from customer pain points and feeds these into process or control improvements while operating within policy, risk and regulatory frameworks
Technical Capabilities
Legal, Regulatory Compliance:  Supports AML‑related reviews by gathering information, completing analysis, and documenting findings under supervision, adhering to policy, risk and understanding regulatory requirements.
Technical Communication:  Communicates information clearly and accurately, with guidance on structure and messaging

title: Regulatory Reporting Analyst
description:
At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions, enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed in the right ways, all more confidently and more often—that’s what we call the courage to thrive.   We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.
  
 As a wholly owned subsidiary of U.S. Bank, Elavon is committed to building the platforms and ecosystems that help over 1.5 million customers around the world to achieve their financial goals—no matter what they need. From transaction processing to customer service, to driving innovation and launching new products, we’re building a range of tailored payment solutions powered by the latest technology. As part of our team, you can explore what motivates and energizes your career goals: partnering with our customers, our communities, and each other.
  
 We actively uphold transparent and fair hiring practices that support individual opportunity, inclusive culture, and career mobility across all levels of our organisation.
 
 We offer meaningful opportunities for growth, a culture of inclusion, and a strong commitment to transparency and integrity in everything we do.
 
 
 
 Job Description Key Responsibilities 
 
 Regulatory Reporting Production & Review 
 Assist the preparation, review and submission of regulatory returns across U.S. Bank Europe DAC and associated European entities.

 Ensure submissions are completed accurately and within regulatory deadlines.

 Perform detailed reconciliations and analytical reviews between regulatory returns, general ledger balances, risk systems and management information.

 Investigate and resolve reporting discrepancies, data quality issues and validation exceptions.

 
 Regulatory Interpretation & Change Management ​ 
 Support the interpretation and implementation of new regulatory requirements issued by:
 

 European Banking Authority (EBA)

 European Central Bank (ECB)

 Central Bank of Ireland (CBI)

 Local European regulators

 Assess the impact of regulatory changes on existing reporting processes and systems.

 Participate in regulatory reporting projects including CRR/CRD developments, taxonomy upgrades, system enhancements and business change initiatives.

 Contribute to regulatory reporting framework enhancements and control improvements.

 
 
 Governance & Controls 
 Maintain a strong control environment supporting all reporting activities.

 Ensure procedures, methodologies and control evidence are properly documented.

 Support internal audits, external audits and regulatory reviews.

 Prepare evidence and documentation required for governance committees and regulatory examinations.

 Escalate material issues and risks in accordance with established governance processes.

 
 Data Management & Analysis 
 Analyse large data sets to identify trends, anomalies and reporting impacts.

 Partner with Data Governance, Finance, Risk and Technology teams to improve data quality.

 Support implementation of data lineage, data controls and data governance initiatives.

 Develop management information and reporting metrics to enhance oversight of regulatory processes.

 Utilise technology and automation tools to improve reporting efficiency and reduce operational risk.

 
 Qualifications & Experience Essential 
 3+ years' experience within:

 Regulatory Reporting

 Financial Reporting

 Treasury Reporting

 Risk Reporting

 Banking Finance

 Strong understanding of prudential banking regulations and reporting requirements.

 Advanced Excel skills / Data Management Skills.

 Experience performing reconciliations, control reviews and analytical assessments.

 Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

 Strong organisational skills and ability to manage competing deadlines.

 Bachelor's degree in accounting or finance, or equivalent work experience

 
 Skills & Experience 
 Experience with COREP, FINREP, LCR, NSFR or statistical reporting.

 Experience with regulatory reporting systems and data warehouses.

 Knowledge of SQL, Power BI, Alteryx, Python or other analytical tools.

 Experience working with European banking regulators.

 Knowledge of CRR, CRD, EBA reporting frameworks and ECB supervisory expectations.

 
 This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. 
 
 Accessibility 
 We are committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruitment experience. If you need adjustments at any stage of the application or hiring process, please contact your recruiter for guidance and support. 
 
 Total Rewards 
 U.S. Bank is committed to fair, equitable, and transparent compensation practices in line with local regulatory and legal requirements. Our total rewards approach is designed to attract, retain, and support top talent while ensuring equal pay for work of equal value.
  
 We offer a market-competitive compensation package that includes:
 Clearly defined salary ranges aligned with industry benchmarks and internal equity standards.

 Performance-based incentives for eligible employees (as defined by relevant plan rules), awarded through transparent, objective criteria that recognize both individual and company performance.

 Inclusive equitable benefits that are accessible to all employees and focused around our 3 main pillars of financial wellbeing, health & wellness).

 Continuous development opportunities including training, education support, and career progression pathways based on inclusive and transparent criteria.

 Employee recognition programs that celebrate achievements and milestones for all.

  
 We regularly review our compensation and benefits to ensure they remain competitive, inclusive, and responsive to employee needs and market trends. Further details of the compensation package will be provided upon application.
 
 We encourage candidates to explore the full value of our offer, including monetary and non-monetary benefits, at Employee benefits and development | U.S. Bank | Elavon .
   
 Closing Date 
 Posting may be closed earlier due to high volume of applicants.
  
 We aim to provide timely updates throughout the process and encourage early applications to ensure consideration.

title: 2027 Advisory Graduate Programme – Dublin
description:
Graduate Programme 2027 - Build your future in Advisory  
 Advisory work is rarely confined to one discipline. Our clients come to us with complex, connected challenges, and our teams bring together commercial, financial, digital, risk and transformation expertise to help solve them. We work with organisations at every stage of their business journey, from growth and transformation to transactions, risk management, technology adoption, financial reporting and operational improvement.  
 That means graduates can build transferable skills from the outset, while still indicating where their interests and strengths may best fit across Advisory.
 Applying to Advisory 
 You will submit one application to the Advisory Graduate Programme and select your choice of capability preference. This helps us understand where your interests lie while allowing us to consider your skills, strengths and aspirations.
 Capability Preferences 
 Transactions – Deal Advisory, M&A, Restructuring & Recovery, Valuations, Transaction Support and Aviation Advisory
 Management Consulting – Strategy, Transformation Excellence, Change Programs, Workforce Management
 AI, Data & Technology – Data Governance and Responsible AI, Analytics, System Strategy & Implementation
 Accounting – Financial Reporting, statutory reporting, transaction accounting and finance transformation
 Cyber & Risk – Cyber, AML, Internal Audit, IT Risk, Regulatory Compliance
 Quants and Actuarial – Quantitative Risk Advisory, Insurance & Actuarial
 Transactions 
 Help clients make confident decisions during some of the most important moments in their business journey.
 Support financial and commercial due diligence engagements
 Assist with mergers, acquisitions, disposals and fundraising projects
 Contribute to business valuations and financial modelling
 Support restructuring and recovery assignments
 Analyse financial and operational performance
 Prepare reports, presentations and client deliverables
 Support aviation-related advisory and finance projects
 This pathway may suit graduates who enjoy commercial analysis, finance, problem-solving and fast-paced project environments
  
 Management Consulting 
  
 Help organisations turn strategy into action and deliver meaningful change.
 Support business transformation and change programmes
 Participate in stakeholder workshops and client engagements
 Conduct business research and structured analysis
 Assist with programme and project management
 Identify opportunities for process and operating-model improvement
 Develop presentations, reports and recommendations
 Support organisational and workforce transformation initiatives
 This pathway may suit graduates who enjoy problem-solving, communication, storytelling, collaboration and working across industries.
  
 AI, Data & Technology 
  
 Help organisations use technology, data and AI to create better business outcomes.
 Support data analytics, reporting and insight initiatives
 Assist in developing dashboards and management information solutions
 Work with Power BI and Microsoft technologies
 Support data governance and data-quality programmes
 Contribute to responsible AI-enabled business transformation
 Assist with digital and technology-enabled process improvement
 Translate business needs into practical technology and data solutions
 This pathway may suit graduates interested in data, analytics, technology, engineering, innovation and business problem-solving. Technical qualifications are welcomed, but curiosity and willingness to learn are also important.
 Accounting  
  
 Help organisations navigate complex financial reporting, accounting and finance-transformation challenges.
 Support accounting and financial-reporting assignments
 Assist clients with statutory reporting matters
 Help prepare and review financial statements
 Conduct accounting and regulatory research
 Support finance-transformation initiatives
 Assist with the implementation of new accounting standards
 Contribute to transaction-related accounting projects
 Analyse financial information and business performance
 This pathway may suit graduates interested in accounting, finance, reporting and commercial problem-solving.
 Cyber & Risk 
  
 Help organisations manage uncertainty, strengthen governance and build resilience.
 Support internal-audit and assurance engagements
 Assist with enterprise risk-management projects
 Participate in risk assessments and control reviews
 Support governance, compliance and regulatory initiatives
 Analyse business, operational and risk information
 Contribute to cyber-risk and operational-resilience programmes
 This pathway may suit graduates interested in risk, investigation, technology, governance, regulation and how organisations operate.
 Quants & Actuarial  
  
 Help organisations understand complex financial, insurance and risk challenges through data, modelling and actuarial insight.
 Develop quantitative solutions to complex risk measurement questions
 Contribute to actuarial and insurance advisory engagements
 Analyse business, financial and risk data.
 Prepare reports, presentations and recommendations for clients.
 This pathway may suit graduates interested in mathematics, statistics, actuarial science, finance, insurance, regulation and solving complex problems through quantitative analysis.
 As a graduate within Advisory, you will benefit from 
 Exposure to diverse client projects across industries
 Structured learning and career-development opportunities 
 Dedicated coaching, mentoring and peer support
 Professional qualification support where relevant
 Early responsibility and client interaction
 Opportunities to collaborate across Advisory and the wider firm
 Access to national and international colleagues and expertise
 Who We're Looking For 
  
 We are looking for curious, ambitious and collaborative graduates from a wide variety of academic backgrounds. Successful candidates will demonstrate:
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
 Clear written and verbal communication
 Intellectual curiosity and a willingness to learn
 Commercial awareness and sound judgement
 Attention to detail and commitment to quality
 Ability to work effectively within teams
 Adaptability and resilience
 A genuine interest in helping organisations solve complex challenges
  
 It would also be helpful if you have 
  
 Experience gained through an internship, part-time role, volunteering, university society or team-based project. Candidates should be on track to achieve a minimum 2.1 degree classification and possess strong IT skills and a desire to develop as a trusted business advisor.
 Join Us 
  
 We welcome applications from a broad range of disciplines. Depending on the capability preference, relevant backgrounds may include business, commerce, economics, accounting, finance, law, psychology, computer science, data science, information systems, mathematics, statistics, physics and engineering. Degree title alone will not determine placement.
 Our graduate experience is designed to support both breadth and depth. Some graduates may gain exposure across different teams, industries and client challenges before deciding where to specialise; others may begin developing deeper expertise in a particular capability, sector or service line from an early stage.
 Whichever path you choose, you will be supported within a collaborative Advisory environment, with opportunities to learn, grow and contribute across a wide range of client engagements and programmes. 
 Location and working arrangement:  Dublin office, primarily office-based.
 Application and selection process 
  
 Apply through link - complete our application form and upload your current CV. 
 Closing date Thursday 22 October 2026. 
 Selection process early November 2026. Start date Q4 2027.  
  
 #LI-KS1

title: Fund Accounting Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) – Officer
description:
Who We Are 
 At State Street, our purpose is to help create better outcomes for the world's investors and the people they serve. We partner with many of the world's leading asset managers, owners, and financial institutions, providing investment servicing, data and analytics, investment research, and trading services.
 Join our ETF Accounting team supporting some of the world's largest and most sophisticated asset managers. As an Officer, you will have the opportunity to lead the delivery of critical services for a growing and dynamic product set, working across global teams, driving operational excellence and helping shape the future of our ETF business. This role offers significant exposure to senior stakeholders, complex investment products and strategic initiatives within one of the world's leading asset servicing organisations.
 
 Why This Role Is Important To Us 
 ETFs are one of the fastest-growing segments of the investment industry, and Fund Accounting plays a critical role in ensuring investors receive accurate and timely valuations every day. As an Officer, you will be responsible for overseeing the successful delivery of fund accounting services for a portfolio of ETF clients, ensuring the highest standards of quality, control and client service.
 This role offers the opportunity to combine technical expertise and management skills while driving operational excellence, supporting business growth and contributing to key strategic priorities across the organisation.
 
 What You Will Be Responsible For 
 •  Oversee daily NAV production and fund accounting activities ensuring all service level agreements, deadlines and control requirements are achieved.
 •   Lead a portfolio of ETF clients and contribute to the continued growth and strategic development of our ETF business.
 •   Act as an escalation point for complex operational, accounting and client issues.
 •  Partner with technology and change teams on strategic projects.
 •  Support talent development through coaching, mentoring and technical leadership.
 •  Monitor capacity, workflow allocation and operational resilience across the team.
 •  Participate in client service reviews and operational discussions.

•  Identify operational risks and control weaknesses, driving remediation activities where required.
 
 What We Value 
 •  Deep understanding of NAV production and ETF products.
 •  Strong leadership presence and accountability.
 •  Excellent client relationship and stakeholder management skills.
 •  Ability to lead through periods of change and operational complexity.
 •  Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
 •  Proven ability to influence outcomes across multiple teams and functions.
 •  Focus on continuous improvement and operational excellence.
 
 Education & Preferred Qualifications 
 •  Bachelor’s degree
 •  Relevant experience in Fund Accounting, ETF Operations, Fund Administration or Asset Servicing. or a comparable environment.
 •  Understanding of ETF fund structures and investment products is preferred.
 •  Prior experience leading operational workflows and managing complex client relationships.
 •  Experience participating in risk reviews and client governance processes.
 •  Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and confidence working with financial data.
 
 What We Offer 
 •  A leadership role within one of the industry's fastest-growing products, supporting many of the world's leading asset managers.
 •  Opportunities to broaden your expertise through exposure to complex products, strategic initiatives and senior stakeholder engagement.
 •  Career development opportunities across Fund Accounting, Asset Servicing and State Street's global organisation.
 •  A collaborative and inclusive environment that encourages innovation, continuous improvement and professional growth.
 
 About State Street 
 What we do. State Street is one of the largest custodian banks, asset managers and asset intelligence companies in the world. From technology to product innovation, we’re making our mark on the financial services industry. For more than two centuries, we’ve been helping our clients safeguard and steward the investments of millions of people. We provide investment servicing, data & analytics, investment research & trading and investment management to institutional clients.
 
 Work, Live and Grow. We make all efforts to create a great work environment. Our benefits packages are competitive and comprehensive. Details vary by location, but you may expect generous medical care, insurance and savings plans, among other perks. You’ll have access to flexible Work Programs to help you match your needs. And our wealth of development programs and educational support will help you reach your full potential.
 
 Inclusion, Diversity and Social Responsibility. We truly believe our employees’ diverse backgrounds, experiences and perspectives are a powerful contributor to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and reach their maximum potential while adding value to both our organization and our clients. We warmly welcome candidates of diverse origin, background, ability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity and personality. Another fundamental value at State Street is active engagement with our communities around the world, both as a partner and a leader. You will have tools to help balance your professional and personal life, paid volunteer days, matching gift programs and access to employee networks that help you stay connected to what matters to you.
 State Street is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer.
 
 
 About State Street 
 Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success.
 
 We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. As an essential partner in our shared success, you’ll benefit from inclusive development opportunities, flexible work-life support, paid volunteer days, and vibrant employee networks that keep you connected to what matters most. Join us in shaping the future.
 
 As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we consider all qualified applicants for all positions without regard to race, creed, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, age, disability, genetic information, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, citizenship, marital status, domestic partnership or civil union status, familial status, military and veteran status, and other characteristics protected by applicable law.
 
 Discover more information on jobs at StateStreet.com/careers

Job Description:
Role Purpose
The purpose of the role is to provide timely, accurate and quality MIS reports, dashboards to the external & internal stakeholders of account(s) as per the defined process and standards of security and compliance
Prepare timely and accurate MIS reports and dashboards as required by the stakeholders
Interact and work closely with management, internal stakeholders & clients to understand the business information needs
Ensuring all reports & dashboards are prepared as per stakeholder requirements as per the desired frequency (weekly/ monthly/ quarterly)
Ensure regular review with the MIS Team Lead for 100% accuracy before populating any customized dashboard or generating any customized report
Track and follow up with relevant stakeholder for timely updation and data management of parameters (key SLA metrics such as run-rate etc.)
Generate account level reports (billable and non-billable) on forecasting, scheduling (both onshore and offshore) and performance against SLAs, CSAT, Quality etc.

Support and adopt tools and systems for efficient MIS generation and reporting system
Continuous support to the manager in rolling out new techniques and initiatives to increase productivity
Providing update to the manager on the progress of any new MIS initiatives
Perform periodic maintenance and servicing of MIS system to improve operational efficiency
Adopt new tools, technology solutions and develop capability through training to improve own productivity.
Develop analytical skills and understanding of statistical analysis to suggest improvement in the quality of analysis

title: Transfer Agency - Dealing, Associate 2
description:
Who we are looking for   

 As an Associate 2 , you will play a key role within the Dealing Services Team, supporting the Officer, Assistant Vice President and senior managers in ensuring client expectations, regulatory requirements, and operational standards are consistently met. You will be responsible for executing and overseeing key processes and controls to deliver efficient, accurate, and high-quality service to clients. This role requires strong knowledge of Transfer Agency Dealing Services, including trade placement, transaction processing, settlement oversight, and associated cash movement activities. Familiarity with Fund Adm inistration and the wider Transfer Agency operating model is highly desirable.   
 

 Why this role is important to us   

 The team you will be joining is part of State Street Global Services (SSGS). SSGS provides asset owners and managers with essential financial tools and operational solutions that support the investment lifecycle. From trade execution support and settlement oversight to fund administration, custody, accounting, and shareholder servicing, our teams play a critical role in ensuring transactions are processed accurately, risks are effectively managed, and clients receive a high standard of service.   

 Join us if you want to make your mark in the financial services industry from day one, working with global clients, and experienced professionals committed to operational excellence and continuous improvement. 
   

 What you will be responsible for   

 As an Associate 2 , you will:   

 Support the Dealing Services team in delivering excellent client service across a broad range of operational activities, including trade placement, trade processing, settlements, cash movement activities, and related Transfer Agency functions.   

 
 Assist with client management to ensure satisfaction with Dealing Services and operational support provided.    

 
 Provide guidance and support to more junior team members as needed.    

 
 Develop expertise in Transfer Agency dealing processes relating to subscriptions, redemptions, trade execution, settlement oversight, and associated cash movements.    

 
 Ensure trades are accurately processed and settled within agreed deadlines while adhering to fund prospectuses, client requirements, and market cut-offs.    

 
 Ensure compliance with regulatory and corporate requirements relating to information security, operational risk, anti-fraud, and other defined standards.    

 
 Contribute to the risk management framework by adhering to controls and escalating issues proactively.    

 
 Participate in department-wide projects and support local team initiatives as required.   

 
   

 What we value   

 These skills will help you succeed in this role:   

 Strong teamwork and communication skills.    

 
 Good knowledge of Transfer Agency Dealing Services.    

 
 Excellent administrative and organisational skills.    

 
 Working knowledge of Transfer Agency operations and fund administration.    

 
 Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple deadlines in a fast-paced environment.   

 
   

 Education & Preferred Qualifications   

 Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (or equivalent experience).    

 
 Experience with relevant tools and systems is desirable.   

 
 Office experience   

 
 Ownership skills   

 

 
 About State Street 
 Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success.
 
 We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. As an essential partner in our shared success, you’ll benefit from inclusive development opportunities, flexible work-life support, paid volunteer days, and vibrant employee networks that keep you connected to what matters most. Join us in shaping the future.
 
 As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we consider all qualified applicants for all positions without regard to race, creed, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, age, disability, genetic information, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, citizenship, marital status, domestic partnership or civil union status, familial status, military and veteran status, and other characteristics protected by applicable law.

title: Data Analytics Graduate Programme
description:
About Allianz: 

We are proud to be one of the world’s most trusted insurance companies, and Ireland’s #1 Property & Casualty Insurer serving over 900,000 customers across Ireland, for over 100 years. Our success is driven by the incredible people we employ, with over 800 people in Allianz Ireland, we are committed to supporting our employees' individual needs and aspirations. 

 

This role is officially based in Elm Park, Dublin 4, but we embrace a hybrid working model that offers you the flexibility and support you need to excel in your role. 

 

We are incredibly proud to be recognised as a Great Place to Work having won the Super Large Category in 2025 & 2026, as well as being named one of Ireland’s Best Workplaces for Women and Best Workplaces for Health & Wellbeing. We are also the proud winners of the Gradireland Best Graduate Recruiter within the Insurance industry 2022 – 2025.  

 

At Allianz, we believe the graduates of today will become the leaders, innovators and experts of tomorrow. If you're ready to take the next step in your career, apply now and become part of the team! 

 

The Data Analytics Graduate Programme: 

The Data Analytics Graduate Programme is a three-year programme where graduates will have the opportunity to build technical expertise, commercial awareness and leadership capability through a structured development journey. 

 

You will gain hands-on experience across some of Allianz's most innovative teams, helping to solve real business problems through data, analytics and technology. Throughout the programme, you will complete four rotations tailored to your strengths, interests and development goals, typically across teams including Data Insights, Transformation, Actuarial, Underwriting, Pricing and other key business areas. 

 

As part of the programme, you'll complete a six-month international assignment within the Allianz Group, giving you exposure to global best practice, different cultures and international career opportunities.  

 

In parallel, you will receive support to achieve your APA (Accredited Product Adviser) professional insurance qualification, benefit from structured learning and development opportunities, and build a strong professional network across Allianz Ireland and the wider Allianz Group. 

 

For more information download our Graduate Programme Brochure 

 

Closing date for applications:  11th October 2026 

 

What we are looking for: 

We're seeking curious, ambitious graduates who are passionate about using data, technology and innovation to solve complex challenges. You may be a strong fit if you:  

  • Enjoy analysing data to uncover insights and support decision making.  

  • Are data driven with an analytical mindset 

  • Have an interest in emerging technologies including Artificial Intelligence and automation  

  • Are naturally curious and enjoy solving problems.  

  • Can communicate complex ideas clearly and effectively 

  • Thrive working collaboratively in cross-functional teams.  

  • Are results oriented & solutions focused 

  • Demonstrate a commitment to continuous learning and professional development. 

 

 

Minimum requirements: 

  • Achieved or expected 2:1 degree in the following areas:  in Actuarial Studies, Mathematics, Statistics, Data Science, Business Analytics, Computer Science, Engineering, Insurance, Artificial Intelligence, or a related field. 

  • Full authorisation to work in Ireland or a valid work permit for minimum of 36-month period covering the duration of the programme.  

  • Demonstrated work experience through internships, placements, part-time employment, volunteering, academic projects or extracurricular activities.  

 

 

Rewards & Benefits: 

  • Competitive graduate salary 

  • Six-month International Assignment 

  • Further Educational Support & Additional Study Leave 

  • 22 Annual Leave Days plus 2 company days and volunteer days  

  • Excellent Health & Pension Benefits 

  • Staff Affinity Insurance Scheme 

  • Hybrid Working Arrangements 

  • Free Lunch 

  • Onsite Gym 

  • Holiday Saving Scheme & Travel Subsidies 

  • Employee Assistance Programme 

  • Active Social Club & Events 

  • Charity and community initiatives   

  • Mentorship Programme 

  • Compressive Learning & Development Support 

 

Allianz plc. is regulated by the Central Bank of Ireland. 

Allianz Group is one of the most trusted insurance and asset management companies in the world. Caring for our employees, their ambitions, dreams and challenges, is what makes us a unique employer. Together we can build an environment where everyone feels empowered and has the confidence to explore, to grow and to shape a better future for our customers and the world around us. 

 

At Allianz, we stand for unity: we believe that a united world is a more prosperous world, and we are dedicated to consistently advocating for equal opportunities for all. And the foundation for this is our inclusive workplace, where people and performance both matter, and nurtures a culture grounded in integrity, fairness, inclusion and trust. 

 

We therefore welcome applications regardless of ethnicity or cultural background, age, gender, nationality, religion, social class, disability or sexual orientation, or any other characteristics protected under applicable local laws and regulations. 

 

Join us. Let's care for tomorrow.

title: Payroll Associate 2027
description:
At Forvis Mazars, we’re not just one of the leading professional services firms in Ireland — we’re a launchpad for ambitious graduates ready to make an impact. With over 1,000 professionals across Dublin, Cork, Galway, and Limerick, and a global network spanning 100+ countries, we offer the scale, support, and opportunities to help you thrive.   
   
 Why join us?  
  
 Our next-generation graduate programme is built around you. We understand that no two people are the same, so we tailor your training, mentoring, and career development to match your strengths, interests, and goals.  
  
 Here, you’ll be more than just a number. You’ll be empowered to lead, innovate, and grow — personally and professionally. If you're looking for a career where your voice matters and your work makes a difference, this is the place for you. 
 
 The Position  
   
 Reporting to the Payroll Manager, we wish to appoint an Associate to work in the Payroll Outsourcing Services department of Forvis Mazars.  Forvis Mazars has a dedicated outsourced payroll bureau that provides payroll service solutions to its clients ranging from multinational companies to owner managed businesses and to public sector bodies.  A full training programme will be provided to the ideal candidate. 
   
 Responsibilities  
   
 Scheduling work to strict deadlines 
 Daily receipt and processing of payroll information 
 Issuing payslips 
 Dealing with client queries  
 Full training program will be provided to ideal candidate.  
 The payroll trainee will report to the payroll manager within the payroll division. 
 Management of time incurred on payroll processing. 
 Filing of Revenue returns online ROS 
 Liaising with clients 
 Liaising with Revenue Commissioners 
 General administration duties 
  
 Ideal Candidate  
   
 Successful candidate must be IPASS qualified or prepared to complete IPASS course as part of their training contract 

 Knowledge of computerised payroll systems 

 Proficient in Microsoft Excel 

 Ability to work effectively to deadlines 

 Excellent communication skills, both written and oral 

 Ability to work on own initiative 

 Meticulous attention to detail 

 Effective organisational skills 

 Ability to work effectively as part of a team 

 Previous payrolls experience an advantage
About you   
   
 We’re looking for bright, motivated individuals from a wide range of backgrounds—whether that’s engineering, business, law, science, or a related field. What matters most is your eagerness to learn, collaborate, and apply your skills effectively. We’ll equip you with the technical and business know-how you need—but your energy, curiosity, and attitude are what will set you apart.  
   
 What we’re looking for   
 You’re working towards or have recently completed an honours degree in any discipline.  

 You act with integrity and always strive to do the right thing.  

 You’re a strong communicator who enjoys meeting people and exploring new ideas.  

 You value respect, inclusivity, and supporting those around you.  

 You thrive in team environments and enjoy working with others.  

 You’re organised, detail-oriented, and able to manage your time effectively.  

 You’re comfortable with technology and have solid computer skills.  

 You think critically and enjoy solving problems with logic and creativity.  

 You have excellent organisational skills, computer literacy and attention to detail

title: 2027 Graduate Production Planning & Scheduling Analyst - Orthopedics
description:
At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow, and profoundly impact health for humanity. Learn more at jnj.com .
 
 As guided by Our Credo, Johnson & Johnson is responsible to our employees who work with us throughout the world. We provide an inclusive work environment where each person is considered as an individual. At Johnson & Johnson, we respect the diversity and dignity of our employees and recognize their merit.
 
 
 Job Function: 
Supply Chain Planning 
 
 Job Sub Function: 
Production Planning & Scheduling 
 
 Job Category: 
Professional 
 
 All Job Posting Locations: 
Ringaskiddy, Cork, Ireland 
 
 Job Description: 
 
 ROLE TITLE: Graduate Production Planning & Scheduling Analyst
 START DATE: September 2027
 LOCATION: Cork, Ireland
 
 Johnson & Johnson announced plans to separate our Orthopaedics business to establish a standalone orthopaedics company, operating as DePuy Synthes. The process of the planned separation is anticipated to be completed within 18 to 24 months, subject to legal requirements, including consultation with works councils and other employee representative bodies, as may be required, regulatory approvals and other customary conditions and approvals. Should you accept this position, it is anticipated that, following conclusion of the transaction, you would be an employee of DePuy Synthes and your employment would be governed by DePuy Synthes employment processes, programs, policies, and benefit plans. In that case, details of any planned changes would be provided to you by DePuy Synthes at an appropriate time and subject to any necessary consultation processes 
 
 DePuy Synthes, Companies of Johnson & Johnson , is the largest, most comprehensive orthopedic and neurological business in the world, built upon the strong legacies of two great companies. 
 
 DePuy Synthes offer an unparalleled breadth and depth of technology, devices, services and programs in the areas of joint reconstruction, trauma, spine, sports medicine, neurological, cranio-maxillofacial, power tools and biomaterials. 
 
 Our broad array of inspired, innovative and high-quality offerings helps advance the health and well-being of people around the world. 
 DePuy Synthes, who employ over 1000 people in Cork established its manufacturing facility in Cork in 1997 where it manufactures orthopedic knees and hips. In 2014, DePuy Synthes in Cork won the Shingo Prize for Operational Excellence.
 POSITION SUMMARY: 
 This role supports production planning and scheduling under supervision, contributing to basic project tasks and process improvements. It involves analyzing trends, managing material availability, and ensuring timely supply to meet production needs. Responsibilities include coordinating supply activities, monitoring performance metrics, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to address constraints. The position also requires effective communication with stakeholders and adherence to company standards.
 
 
 ROLE & RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 Production Planning & Scheduling 
 Help establish and implement programs and innovative initiatives for the Production Planning and Scheduling area, under direct supervision.

 Contribute to less complex components of projects, programs, or processes for the Production Planning and Scheduling area.

 Effectively coordinate the supply planning, purchasing and production scheduling activities for products managed.

 Determine production plan and in association with VS partner, ensures timely completion of planned production.

 Manage on time supply to customers.

 Monitor production planning system with relevant performance metrics e.g. schedule attainment, lead time.

 
 Data Analysis & Process Improvement 
 Complete simple trend analysis to support continuous improvement efforts for the organization's production strategy.

 Analyse product demand, sales patterns, and forecasts, as well as production specifications and plant and supplier capacity data.

 Identify and drive Lean or Six Sigma improvement initiatives.

 Support the evaluation of current processes and the transition to improved future processes in conjunction with the wider global PP&L team.

 
 Material & Supply Chain Management 
 Review shortage reports to ensure materials arrive in a timely manner to meet production requirement.

 Manage raw material and component supply to support Operations.

 Review capacity loads to identify potential manufacturing constraints. Work with Operations, Engineering and Quality partners to resolve and mitigate potential supply challenges.

 Manage and/or maintain raw material inventory investment per inventory entitlement models and drives improvement opportunities.

 Manage supplier performance: measurement, identification of performance issues and working together to resolve and prevent reoccurrence.

 Support evaluation of potential new suppliers.

 
 Cross-Functional Collaboration & Communication 
 Be the key member of relevant New Product launch teams.

 Identify key stakeholders and establish effective communication plans across various groups such as customers, commercial partners, suppliers, global supply chain and site departments.

 
 
 EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE: 
 Essential: 
 Minimum Bachelors degree in Process Excellence/Engineering, Manufacturing or similar engineering/technology bachelors degree, e.g. Supply Chain/Business Information Systems degree 

 Recent Graduate ( 2026  or due to graduate in  2027 )

 Continuous Improvement / Lean Manufacturing systems concept knowledge

 The ability to work well individually and remotely.

 The ability to adapt to change and develop skills to meet these changes.

 High capability with Microsoft Office products (Word, Excel, PowerPoint etc.)

 Interest in developing skills, abilities, and career.

 Pro-active, can-do attitude. High level of personal initiative, ability to function autonomously and self-confidence.

 Self-starter with ability to create and develop new relationships quickly, and influence/collaborate to get to desired results.

 Results Orientation/Sense of Urgency – ability to drive to tight timelines.

 Data mining / reporting skills.

 Exposure to Project Management Methodology would be an advantage

 Interested in Manufacturing processes.

 
 
 
 
  
  
 Required Skills: 
  
  
 Preferred Skills: 
   
  
 The anticipated base pay range for this position is: 
€34,800.00 - €55,775.00  
  
 Benefits: 
 In addition to base pay, we offer the following benefits*: an annual bonus with set target (% of pay) depending on pay grade / location, where the actual amount is based on the employees’ and companies’ performance of the previous calendar year, or sales commissions. Moreover, we offer vacation days, parental leave for a minimum of 12 weeks, bereavement leave, caregiver leave, volunteer leave, well-being reimbursement, programs for financial, physical and mental health. We also offer service anniversary and recognition awards, and subject to the terms of their respective plans, employees - and in some location’s eligible dependents - can participate in several insurance plans. For more information, visit Employee benefits | Supporting well-being & career growth | Johnson & Johnson Careers.

description:
About Allianz 

We are proud to be one of the world’s most trusted insurance companies, and Ireland’s #1 Property & Casualty Insurer serving over 900,000 customers across Ireland, for over 100 years. Our success is driven by the incredible people we employ, with over 800 people in Allianz Ireland, we are committed to supporting our employees' individual needs and aspirations. 

This role is officially based in Elm Park, Dublin 4, but we embrace a hybrid working model that offers you the flexibility and support you need to excel in your role. 

We are incredibly proud to be recognised as a Great Place to Work having won the Super Large Category in 2025 & 2026, as well as being named one of Ireland’s Best Workplaces for Women and Best Workplaces for Health & Wellbeing. If you're ready to take the next step in your career, apply now and become part of the team!  

 

The Opportunity 

As a Personal Accident Claims Handler you will be responsible for managing and processing claims related to personal accidents. The role requires a keen eye for detail, strong communication skills, and the ability to work efficiently under pressure. The PA Claims Handler will ensure that all claims are handled in accordance with company policies and legal guidelines. 

 

Key Responsibilities: 

  • Deliver excellent standards of customer service through high quality and efficient handling of policyholders claims. 

  • Registration, handling and settlement of personal accident claims for a key Allianz account 

  • Accurate and comprehensive recording of all transactions and decisions 

  • Compliance with company quality standards 

  • Compliance with financial services authority requirements for claims handling 

  • Achievement of agreed targets in relation to settlement rate, calls answered and completions 

  • Liaising with others to obtain and deliver information that is critical to service and control of claims costs 

  • Be aware of fraud indicators to identify potential fraud cases and escalate them to the relevant personnel in our Fraud Investigation Unit (FIU) 

 

Key Requirements / Skills & Experience 

Essential: 

  • Minimum 1-2 years’ experience in Insurance Claims handling or Underwriting  

  • APA Qualified or studying towards an APA, CIP or a relevant insurance qualification to meet MCC requirements* 

  • Skilled communicator & negotiator, with ability to work on initiative and manage own time effectively 

Desirable: 

  • Relevant third level qualification 

  • Experience in Claims handling 

 

At Allianz Ireland, we are committed to embracing innovation and the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to drive innovation and business success. We are seeking candidates who demonstrate curiosity, adaptability and have a proactive approach to learning and development. An awareness of AI-powered tools, data-driven decision making and data analysis will be highly valued.

description:
McDermott Laboratories Limited 
 Viatris is a global healthcare company uniquely positioned to bridge the traditional divide between generics and brands, combining the best of both to more holistically address healthcare needs globally. With a mission to empower people worldwide to live healthier at every stage of life, we provide access at scale, currently supplying high-quality medicines to approximately 1 billion patients around the world annually and touching all of life's moments, from birth to the end of life, acute conditions to chronic diseases. 
 
 We have been included on number of award lists that demonstrate the impact we are making. 
 
 Our global portfolio includes best-in-class, iconic brand-name products as well as global key brands; generics, including branded and complex generics; and other offerings across a wide range of therapeutic areas. We are committed to helping create healthier communities worldwide through education, outreach and better access to treatment.
 
 For those driven to live their lives with purpose, Viatris helps employees realise their full potential by creating a collaborative culture that fosters courage and resilience. Viatris is more than just a place to work. This is a place to make a difference in the world.
 
 
 The Role & What You Will Be Doing
 The Global Supply Chain Planning Master Data Analyst is responsible for defining, governing, and maintaining high-quality planning master data across SAP and advanced planning systems in support of global supply chain operations. The role ensures planning data is fit for purpose, supports standardised global processes, and drives effective planning, execution, and reporting — including active involvement in SAP S/4HANA transformation. It requires close collaboration with Planning, IT, Data Quality, and Master Data teams across system deployments, testing, and data migrations.
 
 Every day, we rise to the challenge to make a difference and here’s how the Global Supply Chain Planning Master Data Analyst role will make an impact:
 
 Master Data Ownership & Governance
 Serve as global functional expert for supply chain planning master data across SAP and planning platforms

 Define and maintain end-to-end master data processes covering creation, maintenance, validation, and governance

 Develop and continuously improve policies, standards, and procedures with a focus on data quality and scalability

 SAP S/4HANA & Transformation
 Lead SAP S/4HANA data readiness, planning master data harmonisation, and support for new data models

 Support data migration, cutover activities, and post-go-live stabilisation

 Execute test scenarios and scripts across SIT and UAT phases

 Data Quality & Continuous Improvement
 Define and monitor data quality KPIs, dashboards, and scorecards

 Drive continuous improvement initiatives across data, processes, and systems

 Collaborate with stakeholders across supply chain, manufacturing, IT, and commercial teams to align planning data with business needs

 
 About Your Skills & Experience
 For this role, we’re looking for a candidate who has an effective combination of the following qualifications, skills and experiences:
 
 Strong understanding of master data as a strategic enterprise asset.

 Hands-on functional experience with SAP master data within supply chain processes (MM, PTP, OTC).

 Experience supporting data validation, cleansing, and migration activities.

 Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

 Ability to operate effectively in complex, global, transformation-driven environments.

 Bachelor’s degree in a scientific, engineering, IT, or commercial discipline.

 
 At Viatris, we are dedicated to building a truly diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t fully align with every requirement, we still encourage you to apply. You may just be the right candidate for this or other roles.
 Benefits at Viatris
 At Viatris, we offer competitive salaries, benefits and an inclusive environment where you can use your experiences, perspectives and skills to help make an impact on the lives of others. Some of our benefits include the following on top of a competitive salary:
 
 Excellent career progression opportunities

 Work-life balance initiatives

 Bonus scheme

 Health insurance

 Pension

 
 Diversity & Inclusion at Viatris
 At Viatris, diversity and inclusion are essential to our mission. The diversity we foster in all aspects of our business can be one of our greatest strengths in redefining healthcare not as it is, but as it should be. If you would like to know more about what diversity, equity and inclusion means to us, please visit https://www.viatris.com/en/Careers/Diversity-and-Inclusion 
 
 Sustainability at Viatris
 Corporate social responsibility is fundamental to the Viatris mission. To learn more about our efforts, please visit https://www.viatris.com/en/about-us/corporate-responsibility

title: Abbott Ireland Operations Professional Development Programme (OPDP) - Ireland
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION: Our Operations Professional Development Program (OPDP) is an entry-level, three-year rotation program designed to offer hands-on experience while promoting personal and professional growth. As a participant from Ireland, you will begin the program and first two rotations in your home country, then you will complete your final-year rotation abroad.  
 
 We currently have a number of open positions on our OPDP Program in Ireland.
 
 Upon completion, PDP participants graduate into their next full-time position in their home country, continuing to grow their career and contributing as an Abbott professional using the foundation of skills, experience and network developed during their time in the program. 
 
 As a OPDP participant you will:   
 Be a regular full-time employee of Abbott and qualify for the same competitive salary and benefits as other Abbott employees.  
 Assume full responsibility and contribute as a functional operation professional. 
 Rotate through three challenging, demanding, and diverse assignments. 
 Develop a well-rounded skill set through assignments in the established learning tracks (see below) for the program. 
 Relocate to various sites around Ireland to experience assignment diversity and operations
 Work within multiple business units during your rotational program at Abbott. 
 Have the opportunity to explore possible crossover assignments within other Operation Programs (i.e. Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Operational Excellence). 
 Be paired with a mentor to assist in the development of your operations career. 
 Create a personalized growth plan to serve as a step-by-step guide towards the experiences, knowledge, and resources necessary to achieve your career goals 
 Obtain training customized to support your individual growth and development. 
 Report to a department manager in each assignment who will oversee your day-to-day responsibilities.  
 
 OPDP rotation overview:   
 In Ireland, the OPDP rotation is based on 12month rotations in the first two of three years. Your rotations will involve working across functional areas - Technical, Operations Planning, Quality Assurance, Project Management and Engineering.  
 No assignment is repeated; each is with a different Assignment Manager 
 OPDP participants starting the program in 05 July 2027 will complete a three-year program with the final international (overseas) rotation ending in June 2030
 
   Requirements:   
 Bachelor’s Degree/master’s in Engineering  (Automation / Mechanical / Electrical / Automation) Biotechnology, Pharmacy, Food Science, Supply Chain (Business Studies with major/minor Supply Chain) or related disciplines (grade 2:1 or higher) 
 Tracking to or have a minimum of 2.1 Grade in your undergraduate course with a track record of outstanding co-curricular activities
 Interest in pursuing a career in Operations – Production, Engineering, Plant Quality, etc. 
 Geographically mobile and willing to do at least one year assignment outside of home country
 Unrestricted authorization to work in home country (within Europe)
 Fluent level of English for written and verbal business communication.
 
 Key Skills 
 Capacity to apply skills and knowledge to address operational challenges and add value to the business. 
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. 
 Strong interpersonal, leadership & communication skills. 
 Eager to learn and has the flexibility and willingness to work on different projects. 
 Previous work experience in internship or co-op work experience would be an advantage 
 
 The closing date for applications is  Friday, 08 October 2026 . However, interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis from the launch of the program. We strongly encourage students to apply as early as possible to avoid missing out on these exciting opportunities.

title: 2027 Audit Graduate Programme - Dublin
description:
Graduate Programme 2027 – Audit 
 Real Opportunities with Grant Thornton's Graduate Programme.
 About Grant Thornton 
 Grant Thornton is one of Ireland's leading professional services firms, with nearly 3,000 people and a global network spanning more than 145 countries. We combine local expertise with international insight to help clients solve complex challenges and achieve sustainable growth. 
 Audit 
 About the Team 
 Grant Thornton's Audit practice provides independent assurance services to organisations across a wide range of industries, helping stakeholders make informed business decisions with confidence. Our professionals combine technical expertise, commercial understanding and industry knowledge to deliver high-quality audits that go beyond compliance.
 The Audit practice comprises Corporate Audit, Financial Services (FS) Audit and Global Statutory Audit teams, providing graduates with exposure to a diverse range of industries, organisations and audit environments.
 Corporate Audit works with clients ranging from large multinational corporations and listed entities to privately owned businesses and rapidly growing entrepreneurial companies.
 Financial Services (FS) Audit supports a broad range of regulated entities, including investment funds, asset managers, aircraft leasing companies, banking institutions and insurance businesses.
 Global Statutory Audit works with multinational organisations to coordinate statutory audit requirements across multiple jurisdictions, collaborating with Grant Thornton member firms around the world to deliver seamless and consistent audit services.
 Our professionals support clients across a variety of sectors, including:
 Technology
 Financial Services
 Aviation and Leasing
 Manufacturing
 Healthcare and Life Sciences
 Retail and Consumer Business
 Real Estate and Construction
 Energy and Infrastructure
  
 As an Audit Graduate, you'll gain hands-on experience from day one, working with a diverse portfolio of clients and developing a deep understanding of how businesses operate. You'll have the opportunity to build strong technical accounting and auditing knowledge while gaining valuable insight into the financial and operational drivers behind business performance.
 Whether working with large multinational organisations, indigenous Irish businesses, high-growth companies or public interest entities, you'll contribute to engagements that help build trust and confidence in financial reporting.
 What You Will Do 
 As a Graduate Trainee within Audit, you'll work closely with experienced auditors and client teams on a variety of audit and assurance engagements across Corporate Audit, FS Audit and Global Statutory Audit.
 You may have the opportunity to:
 Assist in planning and executing financial statement audits.
 Review financial records, business processes and internal controls.
 Analyse financial data and assess audit risks.
 Prepare audit working papers and supporting documentation.
 Perform substantive testing across key financial statement areas.
 Participate in stock counts and other audit procedures.
 Support the identification and assessment of control weaknesses and business risks.
 Work directly with clients to gather information and understand their operations.
 Prepare reports, presentations and client deliverables.
 Collaborate with colleagues across Audit, Tax and Advisory teams.
  
 The Experience You Will Gain 
  
 You'll gain practical experience working with businesses of varying sizes and complexities while developing a strong understanding of accounting standards, regulatory requirements and audit methodology.
 How We Will Support Your Development 
 At Grant Thornton, we are committed to helping our people realise their potential.
 As an Audit Graduate, you'll benefit from:
 Structured learning and development programmes.
 Professional qualification support through ACA training.
 Dedicated mentoring and coaching.
 Technical accounting and audit training.
 Study leave and exam support.
 Opportunities to work directly with senior stakeholders and client management teams.
 Access to The Academy training programme.
 Clear pathways for long-term career progression and leadership development.
  
 Our culture encourages curiosity, innovation and continuous improvement, giving graduates the support and opportunities needed to build successful careers in professional services.
 Who We're Looking For 
 We welcome applications from graduates across a broad range of disciplines who are interested in business, finance and professional services.
 Successful candidates will demonstrate:
 Strong IT, analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
 Attention to detail and a commitment to quality.
 Curiosity about how businesses operate.
 A proactive and collaborative mindset.
 Strong organisational and time management skills.
 The ability to analyse information critically and think commercially.
 A minimum 2.1 degree, or expected equivalent, in any discipline. 
  
 It would also be helpful if you have 
 Experience gained through an internship, part-time role, volunteering, university society or team-based project. 
 An interest in how organisations change, improve services or make better use of technology 
  
 Join Us 
 Join Grant Thornton's Audit team and gain exposure to some of Ireland's most dynamic organisations across Corporate Audit, Financial Services Audit and Global Statutory Audit. You'll develop technical expertise, commercial insight and professional skills while helping businesses maintain transparency, accountability and trust.
 Location and working arrangement:  Dublin office, primarily office-based. 
 Application and selection process:  Apply through link - complete our application form and upload your current CV. Closing date Thursday 22 October 2026. Selection process early November 2026. Start date Autumn 2027.

title: Summer Internship Programme
description:
With fraud cases increasing, it is important to be alert and aware. By staying vigilant you can help protect yourself from being the victim of fraud.
2027 Summer Internship Programme
Inspiring Futures: Cantor Fitzgerald Ireland’s 2027 Summer Internship Programme
Cantor Fitzgerald Ireland’s 10 week Summer Internship Programme offers university students a unique and enriching opportunity to explore the world of finance and professional services. Running annually from late May to the end of August, across both our Dublin and Cork offices this structured programme is designed to inspire, educate, and empower the next generation of professionals
Each summer, a select group of interns joins our team for a hands-on experience that blends practical learning, mentorship, and professional development. Interns are immersed in real-world projects, attend interactive workshops, and gain exposure to various departments across the firm. The programme culminates in a final presentation, where interns showcase their work to Cantor Fitzgerald employees, mentors, and invited guests.
What sets our Summer Internship Programme apart is the personalised support and collaborative environment. Interns are assigned dedicated mentors who provide guidance, feedback, and career insights throughout the summer. This close-knit structure fosters meaningful relationships, peer learning, and a strong sense of community.
Beyond technical skills, interns develop essential competencies such as communication, teamwork, critical thinking, and problem-solving. Many participants leave the programme with a renewed sense of confidence, clarity about their career goals, and a valuable network of professional contacts.
At Cantor Fitzgerald Ireland, we are committed to creating an inclusive and supportive environment where students are encouraged to challenge themselves, explore new possibilities, and realise their potential—whether in finance or beyond.
2027 Internship Programme Key Dates
Application form here
Programme Duration: 10 weeks
Location: Cantor Fitzgerald Ireland Offices
Applications open : 31st August 2026
Applications close: 18th October 2026
Highlights of the programme include
Anti-Money Laundering
The Stock Market

2025 Internship Highlights
“During my internship at Cantor, I had the opportunity to gain a well-rounded and immersive experience across multiple departments. A series of insightful talks from the CEO, COO, and employees from various teams provided a deeper understanding of the firm’s operations, culture and general pathway to success. I participated in engaging events, including a meet-and-mingle lunch, a town hall, and a summer party, which fostered a strong sense of community and networking. I attended a training outing at the Bloomberg office and had access to the Bloomberg Terminal, which helped build my technical proficiency and knowledge of markets. A structured rotation through different departments allowed me to broaden my exposure and better understand the firm’s functions. I also had the opportunity to develop and present two project pitches. Within the Corporate Finance department, I took part in high-level industry events such as talks at Mansion House, Dublin Chambers, and Rabobank. I was actively involved in ongoing projects and internal meetings—often treated as a full team member rather than an intern, which was both empowering and motivating. Cantor’s smaller team structure meant that interns were given individual placements and more direct responsibilities, allowing for a more hands-on and involved experience compared to larger firms.”
David Dunne, 2025 Corporate Finance Intern

title: Motor Claims Handler
description:
By joining Sedgwick, you'll be part of something truly meaningful. It’s what our 33,000 colleagues do every day for people around the world who are facing the unexpected. We invite you to grow your career with us, experience our caring culture, and enjoy work-life balance. Here, there’s no limit to what you can achieve.
 
 
Motor Claims Handler 
 
 Job Location: Ireland – Home working Job Type: Permanent Remuneration : Competitive salary taking into account skills, experience and qualifications  
 Join our Motor Division as a Claims Handler, managing a portfolio of motor damage claims for key clients. 
 As a Motor Claims Handler, you'll take ownership of a portfolio of motor files. You will be required to assess both liability and quantum, determine coverage and manage your assigned claims in an expedient, compliant and customer-focused way.
 
 We're looking for someone with  experience in managing  motor claims, ideally gained in a similar motor claims environment. We are looking for someone to join this fast growing team who is looking for opportunities to develop personally and is able to contribute to improving the overall performance of the team.
 
 The skills you will have when you apply: 
 Claims Portfolio Management – Essential experience managing motor claims in accordance with SLAs and KPIs.
 Insurance Qualifications – APA qualification is a minimum requirement, ideally the candidate will have CIP and progressing with further qualifications.
 Technical Claims Knowledge – The ideal candidate will have knowledge of how to assess both liability and quantum, the investigations to be undertaken and a good understanding of motor coverages generally. .
 Investigation & Decision Making – Confident carrying out desktop liability investigations, reviewing evidence, determining liability and making accurate, well-reasoned decisions.
 Customer, Client & Complaint Handling – Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a customer-focused approach, confidence liaising with clients and colleagues, and complaint handling experience considered advantageous.
 Negotiation & Claims Resolution – Strong negotiating, influencing and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate and settle claims in a timely, compliant and commercially aware manner.
 Attention to Detail & Accuracy – High levels of accuracy and attention to detail when reviewing documentation, assessing claims and maintaining records.
 Adaptability & Resilience – Able to thrive in a dynamic and target-driven environment, managing deadlines, changing priorities and business needs with a positive and flexible approach.
 
 What we’ll give you for this role: 
 Bonus/incentive scheme
 20 days' annual leave entitlement
 Bike to Work Scheme
 Tax Saver Travel Scheme 
 Discounted onsite Gym Membership (Dublin 4)
 Discounted onsite Montessori (Dublin 4)
 EAP – Employee Assistance Programme
 Life Cover
 PHI – Permanent Health Insurance
 Exams & Professional Membership Fees
 Professional and personal development opportunities
 
 This isn't just a position, it's a pivotal role in shaping our industry 
 At Sedgwick, you'll help people and businesses recover when the unexpected happens, working alongside some of the most trusted names in insurance.
 From day one, you'll have access to learning and development opportunities, including professional qualifications through our partnership with the Insurance Institute, helping you grow your skills and build a rewarding long-term career.
 You'll join a team that's passionate about making a difference, where every role contributes to our shared purpose of caring for people and helping businesses recover.
 
 Next steps for you: 
 Think we'd be a great match? We'd love to hear from you – apply today. 
 
 If you're unsure whether you meet every requirement, we still encourage you to apply. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences. Sedgwick is committed to creating an inclusive workplace and does not tolerate discrimination of any kind. We welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates. Following the closing date, applications will be reviewed and shortlisted candidates will be invited to interview, either virtually or in person.
 
 Sedgwick Ireland is regulated by the Central Bank of Ireland (CBI). This role is subject to the Minimum Competency Code (MCC) as set out by the CBI. This code sets out the minimum professional standard for any person providing certain financial services, in particular when dealing with consumers. This role is classified as a Controlled function (CF5) and is subject to Fitness and Probity Standards, including the requirements outlined in the Individual Accountability Framework Act 2023. Successful candidates will receive training in relation to all regulatory requirements applicable to them.   #LI-REMOTE

title: Audit Associate Galway 2027
description:
At Forvis Mazars, we’re not just one of the leading professional services firms in Ireland — we’re a launchpad for ambitious graduates ready to make an impact. With over 1,000 professionals across Dublin, Cork, Galway, and Limerick, and a global network spanning 100+ countries, we offer the scale, support, and opportunities to help you thrive.   
  
 Why join us  
 Our next-generation graduate programme is built around you. We understand that no two people are the same, so we tailor your training, mentoring, and career development to match your strengths, interests, and goals.   
   
 Here, you’ll be more than just a number. You’ll be empowered to lead, innovate, and grow — personally and professionally. If you're looking for a career where your voice matters and your work makes a difference, this is the place for you.  
 
 The Position    
   
 Auditors have the responsibility of determining how honest and accurate a business’s financial records are while also suggesting ways to reduce cost, enhance revenue and increase profits. As an Audit Associate with Forvis Mazars, you will gain a wide range of experience across a wide variety of clients including privately owned businesses, large corporates, and multinational organisations.  
   
 Forvis Mazars Audit & Assurance teams are split into specific areas; Public Interest Entities (PIE), Privately Owned Business (POB) and Financial Services (FS). Each area offers graduates the opportunity to pursue either ACA or ACCA professional qualification.  
   
 From the outset, you will experience auditing some of the lower risk audit areas and as you progress you will become responsible for the most complex and high-risk sections on an audit file and be pivotal to managing our client relationships and service delivery. The level of your responsibilities will be driven by your capability, your on-the-job performance and your motivation to succeed.
We’re looking for bright, motivated individuals from a wide range of backgrounds—whether that’s engineering, business, law, science, or a related field. What matters most is your eagerness to learn, collaborate, and apply your skills effectively. We’ll equip you with the technical and business know-how you need—but your energy, curiosity, and attitude are what will set you apart.  
   
 What we’re looking for  
 You’re working towards or have recently completed an honours degree in any discipline. 

 You act with integrity and always strive to do the right thing. 

 You’re a strong communicator who enjoys meeting people and exploring new ideas. 

 You value respect, inclusivity, and supporting those around you. 

 You thrive in team environments and enjoy working with others. 

 You’re organised, detail-oriented, and able to manage your time effectively. 

 You’re comfortable with technology and have solid computer skills. 

 You think critically and enjoy solving problems with logic and creativity. 

 You have excellent organisational skills, computer literacy and attention to detail
