title: Statistician
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION: Abbott in Ireland 
 Operating since 1946, Abbott serves the Irish market with a diverse range of healthcare products. We employ around 6,000 people across ten sites in Dublin, Donegal, Clonmel, Cootehill, Galway, Kilkenny, Longford, and Sligo. Abbott Ireland Diabetes Care Division Donegal: Located in Donegal Town, our Diabetes Care division manufactures FreeStyle blood glucose test strips and sensors, including the FreeStyle Precision, FreeStyle Lite, and FreeStyle Libre systems. 
 
 Abbott Ireland Diabetes Care Division Donegal 
 The Abbott Diabetes Care division based in Donegal Town manufactures FreeStyle blood glucose test strips and FreeStyle Sensors for use in diabetes management. Among Abbott Diabetes Care leading brands are the FreeStyle Precision, FreeStyle Lite and FreeStyle Libre system.
 
 Please note any offer of employment for this position is   conditional upon the successful completion   of a pre-employment medical examination, including drug and alcohol screening, conducted by a medical practitioner designated by the Company 
 
 Job Specification 
 Ability to independently data mine multiple large, complex datasets to answer specific research / investigation questions. Curiosity to dig deeper and access other documentation sources to understand the data.

 Provide real time data analysis support to manufacturing in terms of process adjustments, material performance, investigations, programming and yield analysis.

 The ability to strategically interpret statistical findings into a business significant context.

 Provide consulting on data analysis and statistical tools in support of trend analysis, root cause analysis, failure investigation, risk assessment, data management and data visualization to junior team members and engineers.

 Support technical investigations performed within the manufacturing unit.

 Assist with the introduction of analytical test methods & development trials (analysis of variance, setting acceptance criteria & capability analysis) and support efforts to reduce measurement variability.

 Work with scientists and engineers to introduce new machines, materials and processes, inputting into the design of experiments and analysis of resultant data.

 Independently manages multiple projects working with stakeholders to define business questions, timelines and objectives.

 Highly effective in presenting and communicating statistical results to various levels of personnel is required regularly.

 
 Requirements: 
 Bachelor's Degree or higher in a quantitative field (i.e. Mathematics, Data Science, Statistics, Applied Statistics, Biostatistics etc.) preferred.

 Minimum of 4 years experience in a similar role.

 Proficient in a programming language such as python, R, SAS, JMP or similar.

 An understanding of probability, statistical process control, hypothesis testing, non-parametric statistics, time series analysis, linear and logistic regression etc.

 Experience with relational databases (for example: Oracle Databases, MySQL, Microsoft Access, etc.).

      
 The base pay for this position is 
N/A In specific locations, the pay range may vary from the range posted.

 WORK SHIFT: Ie - Dl39S8 (Ireland)

 SIGNIFICANT WORK ACTIVITIES: Not Applicable

Description 
 
 Join us as a Client Service Advisor within our Corporate Risk and Broking line of business, based in our Limerick office and working in a hybrid environment. 

WTW is one of Ireland’s leading insurance brokers, risk advisors, pensions and actuarial consultancies. For more than 100 years, we have built a strong reputation for delivering exceptional client service. Within Corporate Risk and Broking, we design innovative insurance programmes for our clients, helping them quantify, mitigate and transfer risk through our specialist industry expertise and deep market knowledge.

We are now seeking a Client Service Advisor to join our team. The primary purpose of this role is to manage a portfolio of clients by performing the broking role and delivering a high standard of client service that supports our objectives across Client, Financials, People and Operational Excellence.

 The Role 

 
 Perform the broking role for an assigned portfolio of clients, managing renewals, claims, mid‑term adjustments and all client queries.

 Deliver excellent client service in a responsive, efficient and friendly manner, ensuring all deadlines and service standards are consistently met.

 Develop an in‑depth understanding of each client's business, culture and insurance needs.

 Identify opportunities to grow and enhance existing client accounts.

 Build and maintain strong and mutually beneficial insurer relationships.

 Follow all company procedures for renewals, new business, documentation and administrative processes.

 Ensure compliance with regulatory, company and market standards at all times.

 Participate in internal project work and contribute to process improvement initiatives.

 Provide technical support to colleagues, assisting in the resolution of client or placement issues.

 Build positive working relationships and collaborate effectively with a variety of local and offshore teams.

 Act as an ambassador for WTW, demonstrating our purpose, values and client‑centric culture.

 

 Qualifications 
 
 What you’ll bring 

 
 Certified Insurance Practitioner (CIP) qualification (or working toward completion).

 Previous experience in insurance broking or within an insurer.

 A strong client‑focused mindset with excellent relationship‑building skills.

 Proactive approach with the ability to take initiative and responsibility early on.

 Interest in expanding knowledge of the insurance industry and market dynamics.

 Strong analytical, organisational and communication skills.

 High level of accuracy and attention to detail in all tasks.

 Ability to work both independently and as part of a collaborative team.

 Proficiency in Microsoft Office and confidence with IT systems.
 

 
 What we offer

You'll also benefit from a €1,500 health insurance allowance, life assurance, future-focused pension contributions, hybrid working options, educational support, employee assistance programme and a fully paid volunteer day to make a difference in your community.  On top of these, you can opt into a variety of additional perks including our share scheme, cycle-to-work programme, dental, critical illness protection, enhanced optical cover, and much more. Start making the most of your career and wellbeing with a range of benefits tailored for you.

 Equal Opportunity Employer 
We’re committed to equal employment opportunity and provide application, interview and workplace adjustments and accommodations to all applicants. If you foresee any barriers, from the application process through to joining WTW, please email candidatehelpdesk@wtwco.com

title: Transaction Analyst
description:
Transaction Analyst 
 Full-time, Permanent 
 Hybrid - 3 Days Onsite 
 Monday – Friday, 9am – 5.30pm 
 Dublin, Ireland 
   
 The Position 

 We are seeking a detail-oriented and proactive Transaction Analyst to join our team in Dublin. Working alongside the Cash Management Senior Analysts, you will support the coordination and oversight of complex transactions from a governance, compliance, and administrative perspective. 
  
 This role offers exposure to a wide range of treasury and cash management activities, including trade validation and settlement, cash reconciliations, waterfall/IPD reporting, and stakeholder management. You will work closely with internal teams, clients, investors, legal counsel, and other transaction parties to ensure transactions are executed accurately, efficiently, and within market deadlines.  
  
 This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to build a career in transaction management, treasury operations, and structured finance within a dynamic and collaborative environment. The salary range for this role is €35,000 – €45,000. The final salary will be determined based on relevant skills, experience, and role scope, in line with our objective and gender ‑ neutral compensation framework. 
   
 Key Responsibilities 
  
 Work within the Specialist Services division of Global Capital Markets based in Dublin to assist in the coordination and oversight of transactions from a governance, compliance and administrative perspective, including review of legal documentation as well as liaising with investors, arrangers, lawyers and other transaction parties. 
 Settlement of the confirmed trades referred to above within market deadlines. 
 Authorisation of approved settlements and other payments. 
 Reconciliation of daily bank statements and follow up with counterparties on unreconciled items. 
 Assist Senior Analysts with the management of bank account cash positions and preparation of relevant Cash Management Reports relevant to transactions. 
 Liaising with other in-house departments and external clients to ensure accurate and timely settlement of all transactions. 
 IPD and Waterfall Calculations- developing and maintaining waterfall/IPD reporting through lifecycle of transaction. 
 Input, validation and confirmation of a range of Treasury related products including loan rollovers, money market deposits, interest rate swaps, currency swaps, FX trades, repos etc. 
 Participate in any other projects as reasonably required by the business. 
   
   
 What technical skills, experience and qualifications do you need? 
  
 Legal, Finance or Business degree or similar 
 2-4 years' Banking/Financial Services/Capital Markets Experience 
 Knowledge of financial markets and products is essential, as is experience in the use of SWIFT and other payments systems for confirming and settling these products 
 Excellent attention to detail 
 IT Literate 
 Excellent written and oral communication skills 
 Ability to cope with a busy workload 
 Ability to agree and meet deadlines 
 Able to use good judgment to make sound decisions 
 Planning and organisational skills 
 Ability to work effectively as part of a team while also comfortable working on own initiative 
 Energetic, enthusiastic and enjoys working in a strong team environment

 Reporting to the Client Services Lead or Senior Manager, you will be responsible for delivering a proactive and client-centric service experience while ensuring adherence to service standards and operational controls. This role offers an excellent opportunity to develop in-depth knowledge of global custody operations and gain exposure to the complexities of international financial markets.
 
 What you'll do 

 Provide high-quality support to clients across Global Custody and Direct Custody products, including Settlements, Asset Servicing, Cash, FX, and Tax.
 Proactively manage and respond to client enquiries received through telephone, email, and other communication channels, ensuring accuracy and adherence to agreed service levels.
 Maintain compliance with global standards for monitoring, recording, and resolving client queries through designated case management systems.
 Manage urgent requests and escalated issues effectively, balancing client expectations with operational requirements and risk controls.
 Build and maintain strong working relationships with internal partners, operational teams, and external clients to support the delivery of an exceptional client experience.
 Support the preparation and analysis of service metrics, management information (MI), and KPI reporting to monitor team performance and service delivery.
 Identify recurring issues through trend analysis and root cause reviews and contribute to the implementation of service improvement initiatives.
 Participate actively in cross-training and knowledge-sharing activities to broaden product expertise and operational understanding.
 Demonstrate a strong commitment to risk management, regulatory compliance, and Citi's control framework by adhering to policies, escalating issues appropriately, and safeguarding client assets and the firm's reputation.
 
 What we'll need from you 
 Previous experience in a customer service, client service, operations, or financial services environment.
 Strong academic background or an equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience.
 Knowledge of custody, settlements, asset servicing, cash management, FX, tax, or related financial market products is advantageous.
 Ability to work effectively in a structured, high-volume, deadline-driven environment while managing multiple priorities.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a keen attention to detail.
 Proven ability to manage urgent matters, client escalations, and stakeholder expectations professionally and efficiently.
 Demonstrated ability to adapt to change and contribute positively in a complex operational environment.
 Self-motivated, resilient, and eager to learn, with a commitment to continuous development and delivering excellent client outcomes.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
 Strong focus on teamwork, collaboration, and delivering a client-centric service experience.
 Bachelor’s Degree/University degree or equivalent experience in Business, Accounting or Finance
 
 
 What we can offer you 
 By joining Citi Dublin, you will not only be part of a business casual workplace with a hybrid working model (up to 2 days working at home per week), but also receive a competitive base salary (which is annually reviewed) and enjoy a whole host of additional benefits that support you (and your family) to be well, live well and save well.
 
 Alongside these benefits Citi is committed to ensuring our workplace is where everyone feels comfortable coming to work as their whole self every day.  We want the best talent around the world to be energised to join us, motivated to stay, and empowered to thrive.

title: IT Systems Analyst - EMEA Change
description:
THE OPPORTUNITY 

 Regulatory and compliance-driven change is the most demanding type of IT delivery: the obligations are externally fixed, the timelines are non-negotiable, and the legacy systems they must change are often poorly documented and highly interconnected. As a Systems Analyst on the EMEA Change Team, you are the person who makes that tractable — translating regulatory obligations into structured, precise requirements that architects and delivery teams can act on.
 You will own the analysis function across assigned programmes, working with compliance, legal, business, and technical stakeholders to produce requirements that are complete, unambiguous, and traceable back to the obligation that created them. You will navigate multi-country complexity, identify cross-system dependencies, and ensure that nothing falls through the gap between what a regulation requires and what the system delivers.
 
 WHAT YOU’LL DO 

 Regulatory & Compliance Analysis 
 Analyse regulatory and compliance obligations — interpreting legislation, regulatory guidance, and internal compliance requirements and translating them into structured IT change requirements
 Identify the full scope of impact across the application estate: which systems are affected, which data flows are in scope, which processes must change
 Distinguish between what a regulation mandates and what is an implementation choice — keeping scope bounded to what is required
 Flag newly identified regulatory obligations as high-priority findings and ensure they receive legal or compliance review before scope is finalised
 Maintain a clear register of regulatory obligations, the requirements they drive, and their traceability through delivery
 Requirements & Structured Analysis 
 Lead structured discovery sessions with compliance, legal, business, and technical stakeholders — translating intent into unambiguous functional requirements
 Manage requirements formally — distinguishing confirmed requirements, provisional requirements, and open questions at all times
 Log every decision (verbal, written, or inferred) in a structured decision register; nothing left informal
 Identify and maintain scope boundaries; escalate scope additions rather than absorbing them into delivery
 Author acceptance criteria in a testable format, ensuring requirements are verifiable without interpretation
 Legacy System & Impact Assessment 
 Analyse existing system documentation — runbooks, interface documents, functional specifications, and security controls — to establish current-state baselines for change impact
 Identify integration and dependency risks: changes to one system that have downstream effects on others, including cross-programme dependencies
 Document gaps in existing system documentation as findings in their own right — absence of evidence is evidence of risk
 Assess the impact of regulatory changes across multiple country instances of the same application, identifying where divergence between instances creates additional complexity
 Support migration and decommissioning planning by providing structured analysis of what a system does, what depends on it, and what must be preserved or replaced
 Cross-Country & Multi-Programme Coordination 
 Manage analysis across multiple concurrent regulatory programmes, prioritising and sequencing work with the delivery manager
 Coordinate requirements across EMEA country teams — identifying where a single regulatory obligation has different implementation implications in different jurisdictions
 Maintain awareness of cross-programme dependencies and escalate conflicts or sequencing risks to the delivery manager before they affect delivery
 Produce clear, well-structured documentation suitable for review by non-technical compliance and legal stakeholders as well as delivery teams
 AI-Assisted Analysis 
 Use AI tooling to accelerate document analysis, gap assessments, and specification drafting — applying judgement to review, validate, and correct AI-generated outputs before they are used
 Contribute to the team’s AI-assisted analysis capability — identifying where tooling can reduce manual effort and sharing effective approaches with colleagues
 Collaboration 
 Partner with architects on technical impact assessments and integration design — providing the requirements context they need to make sound architectural decisions
 Collaborate with delivery managers on programme planning — providing effort estimates, dependency maps, and risk flags that inform delivery schedules
 Work with QA and testing teams to ensure requirements are complete enough to produce meaningful test cases, and that acceptance criteria are directly testable
 Engage directly with compliance, legal, and business stakeholders to validate requirements before delivery begins — owning the sign-off cycle
 
 At AIG, we value in-person collaboration as a vital part of our culture, which is why we ask our team members to be primarily in the office. This approach helps us work together effectively and create a supportive, connected environment for our team and clients alike. 
 
 Enjoy benefits that take care of what matters 
 At AIG, our people are our greatest asset. We know how important it is to protect and invest in what’s most important to you. That is why we created our Total Rewards Program, a comprehensive benefits package that extends beyond time spent at work to offer benefits focused on your health, wellbeing and financial security—as well as your professional development—to bring peace of mind to you and your family.
 
 Reimagining insurance to make a bigger difference to the world 
 American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a global leader in commercial and personal insurance solutions; we are one of the world’s most far-reaching property casualty networks. It is an exciting time to join us — across our operations, we are thinking in new and innovative ways to deliver ever-better solutions to our customers. At AIG, you can go further to support individuals, businesses, and communities, helping them to manage risk, respond to times of uncertainty and discover new potential. We invest in our largest asset, our people, through continuous learning and development, in a culture that celebrates everyone for who they are and what they want to become.
 
 Welcome to a culture of inclusion 
 We’re committed to creating a culture that truly respects and celebrates each other’s talents, backgrounds, cultures, opinions and goals. We foster a culture of inclusion and belonging through learning, cultural awareness activities and Employee Resource Groups (ERGs). With global chapters, ERGs are a cornerstone for our culture of inclusion. The talent of our people is one of AIG’s greatest assets, and we are honored that our drive for positive change has been recognized by numerous recent awards and accreditations.
 
 AIG provides equal opportunity to all qualified individuals regardless of race, color, religion, age, gender, gender expression, national origin, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected categories. 
 
 AIG is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to job applicants and employees with disabilities.  If you believe you need a reasonable accommodation, please send an email to candidatecare@aig.com .  
 
 
 
 
 Functional Area: 
IT - Information Technology 
 
American International Group UK Limited, Ireland Branch & AIG Europe S.A. (Ireland Branch)

At AIB, our values guide how we work and how we support each other. We’re looking for someone who puts Customer First , takes initiative and Owns the Outcome , and is always looking for ways to Eliminate Complexity . You’ll treat colleagues and customers with fairness and Show Respect , and you’ll thrive in a culture built on collaboration where we Be One Team to deliver meaningful impact.
Role: Auditor – Group Internal Audit, Enterprise Delivery
Location/Office Policy:  Molesworth Street, Dublin 2 or Regional Hub (Cork/Galway/Waterford) with Hybrid Working (3 days office based)
Do you have a curious mindset and enjoy analysing risks, controls and business processes?
Are you confident communicating with stakeholders and presenting your observations in a clear and professional manner?
Do you want to build a rewarding career in Internal Audit, gaining exposure to strategic, regulatory and operational risks across the Group?
What is the Role:
Group Internal Audit (GIA) is not your typical audit function. We’re on an ambitious journey to create the best function we can for AIB and our people.  Through our audit charter, we operate independently as the third line of defence to provide assurance to our stakeholders on the adequacy and effectiveness of AIB and its subsidiaries governance, risk management and internal control environment.
Most importantly, we believe that great people are the key to our success. This is why we work hard to build a team of empowered individuals who are driven to excel through collaboration, inclusion and diversity; embracing the unique strengths and insights everyone brings.
We are a group of 100+ professionals operating in Ireland and the UK, who always aim for the highest quality. To get the best from our people we support and embrace flexible working arrangements to provide an empowering environment where people get the job done through managing their own time. GIA is now seeking applications from ambitious professionals who are keen to pursue an opportunity as an Auditor of Enterprise Delivery.
Key accountabilities;
Participate in audits from beginning to end including definition of audit scope, test strategy, execution of testing, summary of issues and final report;
Review and interpret processed data to identify trends and investigate exceptional items;
Communicate effectively with management and staff across the organisation by positively conveying the role and value of internal audit;
Continuous adherence to and improvement of the Internal Audit process; and
Opportunities to get involved in working groups across the department, e.g. Methodology, People, Data Analytics, AI.
What you Will Bring ;
Currently undergoing exams to attain an audit/accountancy qualification or the willingness to undertake such qualifications (e.g. CIA, ACCA, ACA, CIMA, CISA);
A minimum of two years in a financial services and/or audit environment;
Preference for people who have practical experience of providing assurance or who have a working knowledge of the key risks within financial services;
Knowledge of key regulations within the Financial Services industry; and
You’ll have lots of initiative, excellent attention to detail and ability to work to deadlines and remain calm under pressure.
Why Work for AIB:
We are committed to offering our colleagues choice and flexibility in how we work and live and our hybrid working model enables our people to balance their time between working from home and their designated office, subject to their role, the needs of our customers and business requirements.
Some of our benefits include;
Market leading Pension Scheme
Healthcare Scheme
Variable Pay
Employee Assistance Programme
Family leave options
Two volunteer days per year
Please click here for further information about AIB’s PACT – Our Commitment to You.
Key Capabilities
Behavioural Capabilities:
Collaborates
Ensure Accountability
Technical Capabilities:
Auditing
Risk Mitigation
Legal, Regulatory and Compliance
If you are not sure about your suitability based on any aspects of the role advertised, we encourage you to please contact the Recruiter for this role, Nicole Pasquetti at careers@aib.ie  for a conversation.

title: Actuary and Governance Consulting Analyst – Ireland
description:
Company: Mercer 
 Description: 
 We are seeking a talented individual to join our Ireland Consulting Team, part of our People and Investments business at Marsh. This role will be based in Lisbon. This is a hybrid role that has a requirement of working at least three days a week in the office.
 
 As a consulting analyst, you will work as part of a team supporting consultants in all aspects of pensions consulting and governance work on both corporate and trustee clients.
 You will work directly with Ireland-based consultants and manage the delivery of services to our clients.
 
 
 We will count on you to: 
 Support your client team on project management, day-to-day client contact, problem resolution, and supervision of analysts’ work
 Undertake actuarial modelling, spreadsheet modelling and calculations, including valuations, individual calculations, regular updates, actuarial factors and accounting work.
 Supporting in the preparation of Trustee meetings packs;
 Draft and update all the relevant governance documents required under IORP II;
 Collect information to provide to Key Function holders (Internal Audit and/or Risk Manager);
 Prepare and link with the different stakeholders to prepare the governance compliance checklist;
 Liaise with other Mercer business areas to deliver a streamlined service to clients.
 Be involved in ad-hoc project work as required, for example, risk management exercises, ETV projects, redundancy projects, etc.
 Act as a key point of contact for technical and scheme-specific queries received from clients, third parties and other Mercer businesses.
 Support the business in some non-billable task such as billing process, general analysis, etc. 
 
 
 What you need to have: 
 Bachelors or Master’s in Actuarial, Mathematics, Economics, Management, Finance or similar.
 Excellent written and spoken English communication skills.
 Excellent planning and organisational skills in order to prioritise and effectively manage a wide variety of ongoing tasks, in order to meet the multiple deadlines;
 Proven team player with a flexible attitude towards work;
 Ability to multitask, prioritise workloads and sometimes work to tight deadlines;
 Proven ability to deliver excellent client service and satisfaction;
 Strong problem solving skills & ability to clearly articulate complex issues.
 Advanced Microsoft Office skills (in particular a strong working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, and Word);
 Good attention to detail is critical;
 
 
 What makes you stand out: 
 Previous experience in consulting and or actuarial matters
 Strong relationship building skills with ability to work closely with internal teams, customers & sales team;
 Proactive and goal oriented.
 
 
 Why join our team: 
 We help you be your best through professional development opportunities, interesting work and supportive leaders.
 We foster a vibrant and inclusive culture where you can work with talented colleagues to create new solutions and have impact for colleagues, clients and communities.
 Our scale enables us to provide a range of career opportunities, as well as benefits and rewards to enhance your well-being.
 
 
Marsh (NYSE: MRSH) is a global leader in risk, reinsurance and capital, people and investments, and management consulting, advising clients in 130 countries. With annual revenue of over $27 billion and more than 95,000 colleagues, Marsh helps build the confidence to thrive through the power of perspective. For more information, visit marsh.com, or follow us on LinkedIn and X. 
 
Marsh is committed to creating a diverse, inclusive and flexible work environment. We aim to attract and retain the best people and embrace diversity of age, background, disability, ethnic origin, family duties, gender orientation or expression, marital status, nationality, parental status, personal or social status, political affiliation, race, religion and beliefs, sex/gender, sexual orientation or expression, skin color, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. 
Marsh is committed to hybrid work, which includes the flexibility of working remotely and the collaboration, connections and professional development benefits of working together in the office. All Marsh colleagues are expected to be in their local office or working onsite with clients at least three days per week. Office-based teams will identify at least one “anchor day” per week on which their full team will be together in person.

title: Equity Analyst – Fundamental Value Equities - VP1, State Street Investment Management
description:
Equity Analyst – Fundamental Value Equities 
 Location: Dublin, Ireland   
 Team: Active Fundamental Equities  
 Sector: Information Technology & Communication Services
 
 Promoting a Culture of Excellence 

 Our success hinges on attracting the best people. Highly skilled, engaged, and productive teams are our greatest asset — and essential to everything we achieve. We hire talented, diverse professionals who share our commitment to helping clients, and those who rely on them, achieve financial security. We insist on, and reward, performance excellence.
 We are committed to helping you build a fulfilling career. Our aim is to be the employer of choice, offering competitive compensation, meaningful development opportunities, and a work environment that values a diverse range of people, ideas, and skills.
 
 The Company 

 State Street Investment Management is a global leader in institutional asset management, entrusted with more than $6 trillion in assets. We partner with many of the world's largest and most sophisticated investors and financial intermediaries, helping them reach their goals through a rigorous, research-driven investment process spanning both indexing and active disciplines.
 We are passionate about understanding the specific needs of those we serve. By applying deep experience and intellectual rigour across a broad toolkit, we develop and deliver thoughtful, targeted solutions designed to ensure their success — and the success of the millions of people who depend on them.
 
 The Team 

 State Street Investment Management's Dublin-based Fundamental Value Equity Team invests in undervalued equities through bottom-up, value-based stock selection, grounded in rigorous fundamental analysis and a long-term investment horizon. The concentrated nature of our global and regional portfolios ensures that every position is an active, high-conviction investment in what we believe are our most compelling opportunities.
 Role Summary / Purpose

 We are seeking an Equity Analyst to join our Information Technology and Communication Services sector research team. You will be responsible for delivering excess returns through security selection across a global sector, adhering to an investment approach consistent with our long-standing investment philosophy. You will also help advance our research process by thoughtfully integrating AI and other emerging tools to deepen insight, enhance efficiency, and strengthen investment decision-making — while preserving the rigour and independent judgement at the core of our philosophy.
 
 Essential Responsibilities 

 Meet with, analyse, model, and value the equity securities of global publicly listed corporations.

 Collaborate with the global Information Technology and Communication Services sector team to manage the global sector sleeve of our research portfolio.

 Recommend investments for inclusion in our suite of concentrated regional and global strategies.

 Contribute to a culture of continuous improvement across our investment process, models, and tools — including the integration of AI and advanced analytics to enhance research productivity, idea generation, and analytical depth.

 Apply AI-enabled tools to accelerate data gathering, synthesis, and modelling, while rigorously validating outputs to uphold the accuracy and integrity of our research.

 Support client teams and Portfolio Managers with RFPs, presentations, commentaries, and other regular and ad hoc marketing deliverables.

 Partner with the Client Portfolio Manager for Active Fundamental Equity to provide product updates to the EMEA sales teams.

 Become a thoughtful and compelling advocate for our investment approach, both internally and externally.

 
 Basic Qualifications 

 Bachelor's degree, preferably in a business-related discipline.

 CFA, MBA, or an accounting qualification would be an advantage.

 
 Desired Characteristics 

 Significant Information Technology or Communication Services sector expertise — most likely gained as an analyst, or in a corporate strategy or strategic consulting role.

 Excellent financial analysis and valuation skills, combining qualitative and quantitative insight into your research.

 Curiosity about, and openness to, integrating AI and emerging technologies into the investment research process — with the judgement to apply them critically and validate their output.

 Capacity for differentiated thinking and the confidence to challenge the status quo to drive optimal investment decisions.

 A strong collaborator with excellent interpersonal and facilitation skills.

 Strong communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively at all levels of the organisation and to develop and nurture external relationships.

 A genuine passion for investing in companies and markets.

 Initiative and independence, with the aptitude to self-direct and set priorities in a fast-paced environment.

 Curiosity, strong organisation, attention to detail, and a strong work ethic.

 Demonstrated personal and professional integrity.

 
 
 About State Street 
 Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success.
 
 We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. As an essential partner in our shared success, you’ll benefit from inclusive development opportunities, flexible work-life support, paid volunteer days, and vibrant employee networks that keep you connected to what matters most. Join us in shaping the future.
 
 As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we consider all qualified applicants for all positions without regard to race, creed, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, age, disability, genetic information, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, citizenship, marital status, domestic partnership or civil union status, familial status, military and veteran status, and other characteristics protected by applicable law.

title: Engineering Technician - Electrical
description:
Job Description : 
 Shift Engineer   -   Electrical   

 Marshalls Road, Belfast   

 Permanent   

 Closing date:   06/09 /2026   

   

 Shift Engineer -   £ 58,833.73 (including shift allowance)   + competitive benefits package including   up to 14 % pension ,   shares   scheme and   more !   

   

 Join our   Supply   Chain and   Manufacturing   Team   

   

 Our Supply Chain and Manufacturing team are problem-solvers, sourcing, producing, and delivering our much-loved brands to delight customers around the globe. Over half of Diageo’s 30,000+ people work in Supply Chain and Manufacturing.   It’s   an intricate and sophisticated operation   that’s   the product of logistical, manufacturing, and technical collaborations.   
 

 Our teams in 100 sites in over 30 countries cover production facilities, supplier relationships, customer   collaborations   and third-party agreements.   We’re   committed to   realising   our ‘Society 2030: Spirit of Progress’ goals, to protect the environment and support our farmers and suppliers. Whatever your skills and experience,   we’ll   help you to thrive in our inclusive culture.   

   

 
 About the role   

 As a Shift Engineer,   you'll   play a key role in improving line efficiency by minimising unplanned stoppages and improving planned maintenance.   You’ll   lead continuous improvement initiatives, working closely with maintenance teams to ensure quick turnarounds and address recurring issues through root cause problem solving.    

     

 Your focus will be on increasing equipment uptime, driving performance in line with Diageo's standards, and ensuring health and safety compliance. Achieving site and personal KPIs will be a top priority as you contribute to our culture of manufacturing excellence.    

     

 Key responsibilities:   

   

 Contributing to the achievement and improvement of Asset Care KPI’s through the delivery of efficient and effective maintenance, repair, problem solving and improvement of assets and their availability across site .     

 

 Contributing to the achievement and improvement of Asset Care KPIs through efficient maintenance, repairs, and problem-solving.    

 
 Support improvement projects focused on compliance, waste reduction, cash savings, and performance reliability.    

 
 Ensure effective information sharing, handovers, and teamwork, providing technical knowledge and collaborating with OEMs for solutions.    

 
 Manage Planned Preventative Maintenance (PPM) schedules, ensuring   accurate   completion to standards and SAP input.    

 
 Support capital work, including installation, commissioning, and early equipment management; review RCM as needed.    

 
 Work with Operators, Reliability Engineers, and Shift Managers on situational problem-solving using root cause analysis.    

 
 Participate in Daily Tier meetings to address and resolve performance issues.    

 
 Proactively   anticipate   and address issues, driving solutions with the wider engineering team.    

 
 Conduct Daily Craft Inspections and collaborate with Shift Managers to   optimize   machine efficiency and perform repairs during downtime.    

 
     

 Health and safety compliance is key, and   you’ll   be at the forefront of making sure this is   monitored   alongside ensuring both site and personal targets are achieved.    

   

   

 About You   

   

 We're   seeking a   qualified electrical engineer with experience in a fast-paced production or manufacturing environment and a passion for improving asset performance. A proactive problem-solver, you thrive on   identifying   root causes, reducing downtime, and driving continuous improvement while   maintaining   the highest standards of safety, quality, and reliability.   

   

 Recognised Electrical Apprenticeship and Electrical HNC (or equivalent qualification)   

 
 17th or 18th Edition qualified   

 
 Knowledge of v ariable frequency drives. servo drives and motors, Asi bus,   profi bus   and electro-pneumatics.   

 
 PLC fault finding and diagnostic experience (preferred)   

 

 Proven experience in a production, manufacturing, or FMCG environment   

 
 Strong knowledge of electrical maintenance, asset care, and preventative maintenance practices   

 
 Skilled in fault finding, root cause analysis, and implementing effective long-term solutions   

 
 Collaborative team player with a focus on safety, performance, and achieving KPI targets through continuous improvement initiatives   

 
   

   

 Working with Us   

   

 Flexibility is key to our success. From part-time and compressed hours to   different locations , our people work flexibly in ways to suit them. Talk to us about what flexibility means to you so that   you’re   supported from day one.     
 

 We embrace diversity in the broadest possible sense. This means that   you’ll   be welcomed and celebrated for who you are just by being you.   You’ll   be part of and help build and champion an inclusive culture that celebrates people of different gender, ethnicity, ability, age, sexual orientation, social class, educational backgrounds, experiences, mindsets, and more.    
 

 Our ambition is to create the best performing, most trusted and respected consumer products companies in the world. Join us and help transform our business as we take our brands to the next level and build new ones as part of shaping the next generation of celebrations for consumers around the world.    
 

 Feel inspired? Then this may be the opportunity for you.      
 

 If you require a reasonable adjustment, please ensure that you capture this information when you   submit   your application.

JOB DESCRIPTION: The Digital Automation Specialist – Finance is a key contributor to driving digital innovation, automation, and continuous improvement across Finance Shared Services (CFS) in EMEA . Operating within the EMEA Digital Innovation & Automation Centre of Excellence , this role partners with Finance stakeholders, operational excellence teams, and global digital communities to embed scalable, value‑driven automation solutions.
 
 This role blends hands‑on solution delivery with capability building and governance , enabling Finance teams to operate more efficiently, make better decisions, and scale digital best practices across the region.
 
 What You Will Do 
 Digital Governance & Standards 
You will help shape and maintain the EMEA Digital Innovation & Automation COE operating model, ensuring alignment with Business Operational Excellence and global digital standards. You will create and maintain reusable templates, frameworks, and documentation to ensure consistent, high‑quality delivery of automation solutions.
 
 Finance Automation & Capability Building 
You will support the identification and development of digital skills across EMEA Finance, contributing to skills inventories and capability assessments. You will help design learning pathways and actively participate in delivering training, onboarding, and knowledge‑sharing initiatives to strengthen automation maturity across the organisation.
 
 Opportunity Identification & Solution Delivery 
You will evaluate Finance processes end‑to‑end to identify automation opportunities, assess feasibility, and quantify business value. You will design, build, test, and deploy automation and reporting solutions using approved digital tools while ensuring compliance with governance, documentation, and quality standards.
 
 Stakeholder Partnership 
You will work closely with Finance SMEs, BOE leads, transformation teams, and managers to identify high‑impact opportunities. You will facilitate ideation sessions, prioritisation workshops, and value discussions, building trusted relationships that drive adoption and measurable outcomes.
 
 Knowledge Management & Reuse 
You will document proofs of concept, use cases, delivered benefits, and lessons learned, ensuring knowledge is captured in the COE repository. You will maintain visibility of existing digital solutions across EMEA to support reuse and scalability.
 
 Global Collaboration 
You will actively participate in Global Digital and Automation Communities of Practice, sharing insights, reusable assets, and regional perspectives. You will review and adopt solutions developed in other regions, advocating for global consistency while meeting local Finance needs.
 
 Performance Tracking & Reporting 
You will maintain accurate data across COE dashboards and trackers, reporting on pipeline health, delivered automations, efficiency gains, and capability development. You will support leadership with clear, data‑driven insights on digital transformation progress.

 Proven experience delivering digital automation solutions in Finance environments

title: Facilities Engineer
description:
Kepak is a leading food company with 14 manufacturing sites and over 4,500 employees across Ireland and the UK, with a turnover of €1.75 billion. The Group operates across three divisions: Meat Division Ireland, Foods Division and Meat Division UK. Guided by our values—Responsibility, Ambition, Passion for Food, and Teamwork. wWe are committed to operating as a successful, sustainable, future-ready business that is a great place to work. We supply fresh and value-added meat-based products to retail and foodservice through private label and our own brands, including Rustlers, Big Al's and John Stone. 
 
 We have an exciting opportunity for a Facilities Engineer to join our Maintenance team in Cork. This is a full time permanent position reporting to the Primary & Facilities Maintenance Manager. This position will be responsible for the smooth running of our state of the art facilities. Anything from Refrigeration, Boiler, Steam and Energy. You will work cross-functionally across different departments and contractors as well as optimise preventative maintenance schedules.
 
 Key Responsibilities: 
 To ensure supervision and safe operating procedures for visiting contractors, 
 Respond promptly to facilities-related breakdowns to minimise production disruption
 Assist with basic projects such as equipment replacements, upgrades, or energy-saving initiatives.
 To ensure all Compliance service and inspection schedules are completed and actions followed up on
 You will Implement and Drive Continuous Improvement projects ( Self Driven )
 You Work Closely with Operations improving the site assets and the refrigeration performance, availability, and efficiency,
 To assist the Engineering Department in achieving its budget targets through the efficient use of materials and replacement parts.
 Optimisation of the CMMS (Piranha) system regarding asset identification and traceability,
 Assist in emergency breakdown repairs in a timely and efficient way on all Site Facilities equipment and assist across all site engineering issues when required,
 To assist in the installation of new equipment to the site if required.
 Requirements 
 Electrical/Mechanical qualification, HNC or time spent in a Multi-skilled apprenticeship
 Services back-ground / facilities experience ideally within Food manufacturing or high volume manufacturing environment
 CI experience and use of Lean Manufacturing techniques  
 Significant Trouble shooting and fault-finding diagnostics and resolution experience
 Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
 Demonstrate team skills with a positive attitude and professional approach
 Benefits 
 
 Pension Scheme 
 Subsidized Canteen 
 Further Education support - You’ll have clear pathways for advancement, supported by continuous professional development and a range of learning opportunities
 Refer a Friend Scheme - Get up to €500 for successfully referring a friend or family member to Kepak Group.
 Bike to Work Scheme - Purchase a bike and safety equipment through a salary sacrifice scheme which reduces your taxable income – meaning you pay less tax!
 Long Service Awards - We recognise, acknowledge and award the dedication and valuable contribution of long serving employees

title: Clients & Markets Junior Coordinator / Coordinator
description:
To sustain the continuous development of our practice in Italy, we are currently seeking a Clients and Markets Junior Coordinator or Clients and Markets Coordinator to join our team in Milan on a 12-month fixed-term contract (CCNL Commercio, III level) .
 
 Your role 
 Your main responsibilities will include dealing with and managing the relationship with a dynamic team of lawyers operating within a full-service law firm, providing support for its business development and marketing activities.
 
 In particular:
 Drafting and delivering domestic and international pitches/proposals, credentials, capabilities, CVs and presentations. Working on brochures and any other kind of marketing material, also together with the European digital and creative teams to implement the relevant branded collaterals.
 Drafting submissions for Italian and international directories and awards.
 Updating and implementing marketing databases managed locally or by Dentons’ network.
 Providing general support to marketing and communication initiatives and projects, both domestic and international.
 Supporting BD initiatives coordinated by the Italian team or the international network.
 Supporting the implementation and updating of the firm’s CRM tools.
 Requirements 
 • Between 2 and 4 years’ experience operating in a Marketing and Business Development Team in the field of professional services, preferably in an international law firm.
 • Fluent in English (written and spoken). C1 level preferable.
 • University background, in economics/law would be preferable, in addition to marketing education.
 • Flexible team player, with a proactive and problem-solving approach.
 • Ability to work within short deadlines, and to manage priorities and multiple tasks simultaneously.
 • Excellent computer literacy (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Access) on Windows platform. Use of InterAction would be an added value.
 Benefits 
 • 12-month fixed-term contract – CCNL Commercio, III level.
• Gross annual salary (RAL): €32,000 – €37,000, depending on the candidate’s experience and profile.

title: Internation Operations Finance
description:
We have experienced a very high interest for becoming a graduate at Novo Nordisk starting 1 September 2026. The application period ended 7 December 2026. We are reading applications now and first interviews for selected candidates will take place from 16-23 January 2025. Read more about the  application process.
The International Operations (IO) Finance Graduate Programme is designed to develop the next generation of international finance leaders. With offices in 80 countries, the programme ensures ample on-the-job experiences, with the opportunity to bring your finance and business understanding into play in a multicultural network during your international assignments.
Start your career 1 September 2027. Apply here from November 2026. Until then  follow Novo Nordisk on LinkedIn  to get a better feeling of who we are.
Please note that we also offer our Global Finance Graduate Programme.
Novo Nordisk International Operations (IO) is the largest operational unit in Novo Nordisk and covers 194 countries and 95% of the world’s population. IO is split into five regions, spread across every continent of the globe. Employees working within business in Novo Nordisk have a wide range of roles and responsibilities – but all share the same commitment to excellence and to drive continued success of Novo Nordisk.
During the two-year programme you will undertake three exciting and challenging rotations of eight months each, which will include a regional office/business area, affiliate and maybe our International Operations office in Zurich.
You will work as a fully-fledged member of the team and build the competencies relevant to the rotation, all while ensuring a strong financial toolbox and a holistic understanding of Novo Nordisk and the pharmaceutical industry.
An example of an IO Finance graduate’s journey could look like this:
1.     Financial Planning & Analysis, Canada
Engage in the financial planning and finance processes in one of our key affiliates. Gain hands-on experience with Novo Nordisk’ digital and finance tools.
2.     IO Finance HQ, Zurich
Collaborate on diverse business cases that impact our IO markets. Work cross-functionally Pricing, Market Access, and Corporate Affairs.
3.     Regional Finance experience in Denmark, Singapore, Panama or alike:
Product launch support, cross-regional finance projects and get the chance to influence real-life business decisions, gaining a holistic perspective on our operations and strategic initiatives.
We are a successful global pharmaceutical company and the world leader in diabetes care. Your skills, dedication and ambition will help us continue to change lives for the better as we grow our business and help millions of people around the world. Working at Novo Nordisk, you can therefore make a significant difference to patients and society while also delivering exciting results from a business perspective .
During the International Operations Finance Graduate Programme, you will receive comprehensive training to be successful in your role and gain knowledge and an invaluable international experience leading to both professional and personal development . You will develop your core skills within areas such as financial planning & analysis, process management and management reporting. Furthermore, you will work with senior managers and build your global network of world-class colleagues, positioning yourself to be one of tomorrow’s finance leaders at Novo Nordisk.
We’ve designed the program so that, following its successful completion, you will be equipped with the necessary skills and experience to become a valued and promising part of our company within International Operations.
As you embark on your life-changing career in Novo Nordisk, we will provide you with:
Accelerated personal and professional development through one-on-one sparring with a senior mentor assigned to you from day one and an extensive, custom-built training programme
A truly international experience in our many affiliates or regional offices (e.g. Canada, Panama, Denmark, Turkey, Singapore, and many other options)
A unique graduate community spanning across programmes filled with social activities and inspiring colleagues to spare with and learn from.
A competitive entry level salary.
For the positions starting 1 September 2027, we are looking for candidates with:
A recent Master’s degree from 2026 or 2027 There may be some variations in the above requirements depending on country. You can find country specific information in the relevant job advertisement.
Relevant work experience or extracurricular activities obtained next to your studies (max one year between or after studies)
No more than 1 year of full-time work experience between or after completing a Master’s degree
Above average academic achievements
Team-player attitude, excellent communication skills, high drive and an eagerness to learn
Fluent spoken and written English
International experience, for example from studying a full semester abroad, working or volunteering

title: Global Tax
description:
We have experienced a very high interest for becoming a graduate at Novo Nordisk starting 1 September 2026. The application period ended 7 December 2026. We are reading applications now and first interviews for selected candidates will take place from 16-23 January 2026. Read more about the  application process.
The Global Tax Graduate Programme is designed to develop the next generation of Tax leaders. With three rotations across our global tax organisation, the programme will provide you with the opportunity to bring your tax, accounting and business understanding into play to make a difference to patients and society.
Start your career 1 September 2027. Apply here from November 2026. Until then  follow Novo Nordisk on LinkedIn  to get a better feeling of who we are. We welcome applications from all over the world.
At Novo Nordisk, our commitment to sustainability is deeply embedded in the way we manage taxes across the global tax organisation. As part of our sustainable ambition, we are dedicated to managing taxes in a business-anchored, responsible, and transparent manner that supports balanced and competitive tax rates. Our responsibilities include proactively managing tax risks, maintaining open and constructive dialogue with tax authorities to reduce uncertainty, and ensuring compliance with international transfer pricing standards and local regulations.
As part of this approach, we also make use of mechanisms available in relevant jurisdictions to secure competitive tax outcomes in a sustainable and compliant way.
About the Global Tax Graduate Programme
Fast-track to success! This full-time position offers you the chance to experience three exciting jobs in just two years. You will work in various functions across our global tax organisation, with the opportunity of a fast-learning track in different areas and geographic locations - ensuring a strong tax toolbox, including knowledge of digital tools, and a holistic understanding of Novo Nordisk and the pharmaceutical industry.
Working at Novo Nordisk provides the opportunity to make a significant difference to patients and society while also delivering exciting results from a tax perspective.
As you’ll be working towards an ambitious career, we will provide you with:
Accelerated personal and professional development through one-on-one sparring with a senior mentor assigned to you from day one and an extensive, custom-built training programme.
International experience by working abroad for at least eight months in one of our affiliates (e.g., USA, Denmark, Zurich etc.).
Broad and international network of colleagues, chance to work with senior stakeholders and exposure to senior management.
A competitive entry level salary.
Throughout the programme you will gain hands-on experience with transforming data into business insights, with major learnings in the following areas:
1.    Tax Compliance in Pharma : Acquire knowledge of international tax, build Tax Technical understanding, exposure to other business functions
2.    Risk mitigation and reporting:   Risk assessment and methodology experience, mitigation and controls implementation, partnering to drive business value
3.    Digital Processes and Capabilities: Acquire and automation of processes, using technology to improve efficiency, communication, culture and branding
For positions starting 1 September 2027, we are looking for candidates with:
A recent Master’s degree from 2026 or 2027, demonstrating above-average academic achievements within tax, law, economics, accounting or similar
No more than 1 year of full-time work experience between or after completing a Master’s degree
International experience, for example from studying abroad, working or volunteering
Relevant work experience from internships, student jobs, or extracurricular activities, with a maximum of 1 year of full-time work experience between or after completing your Master's degree
Fluency in both spoken and written English
Willingness to relocate globally
You are welcome to apply for more than one track. However, we recommend you to carefully consider which tracks you will apply for and your motivation for doing so. You will have to make an individual application for each programme track and we encourage you to only apply for the tracks that you would be truly excited to join.
Be yourself and share why Novo Nordisk is the company you want to work for. What motivates you and why do you think being a graduate could be amazing. We would like to know who YOU are.
No, our corporate language is English, so speaking Danish is definitely not a requirement. There may be local language requirements for some International Operations (IO) tracks.
Yes, as long as you plan to graduate before the start of the Graduate programme. It is also accepted if you have not received your official graduate diploma before starting in the Graduate Programme, as long as you have finished your studies and are just waiting for the official papers.
This position is designed as an entry-level role, and while many graduates join the program directly after their studies, we also consider candidates with up to one year of post-graduate experience.
Previous pharmaceutical work experience is not a requirement to apply for the programme.
For the Global tracks you will be employed by our HQ organisation and most of the positions will start in Denmark, except for Global Tax, where you will commence your rotations in either Denmark, US or in one of our International Operations locations globally.
For the International Operations tracks you will be employed in one of our specified hiring countries for 2026, where you will undertake your first rotation.
Upon successful completion of the programme, you will be offered a position in Novo Nordisk, therefore full mobility and flexibility is required as the location is not pre-determined.

The Supply Chain Graduate Programme is a two-year programme anchored in our headquarters in Denmark. With rotations in three different Supply Chain areas across the Supply Chain function, you will be provided with the opportunity to build comprehensive knowledge of our value chain and Supply Chain functions in practice. The programme has been designed to develop the next generation of Supply Chain talents who will bring value to Novo Nordisk and make a difference to patients and society. The first rotation will be at the HQ in Denmark.

The Supply Chain organisation is focused on delivering reliable and future-proof end-to-end supply chain planning with the use of digital tools and in close cooperation across the global organisation.
In the role as Supply Chain Graduate, you will develop an understanding that spans across the Global Supply Chain during your rotations. You will work with assignments that provide you with the opportunity to make a direct impact for our patients, create value for our business and work alongside and learn from talented Supply Chain professionals across the globe.

title: Commercial Business
description:
We have experienced a very high interest for becoming a graduate at Novo Nordisk starting 1 September 2026. The application period ended 7 December 2026. We are reading applications now and first interviews for selected candidates will take place from 16-23 January 2025. Read more about the  application process.
The Commercial Business Programme with our International Operations (IO) has been designed to develop the next generation of business leaders and specialists. It will give you the opportunity to make a difference for millions of people who rely on our products.
The two-year Graduate Programme will give you a broad range of invaluable skills and experiences as you work your way across different business areas and countries. Are you one of tomorrow’s key people?
Start your career 1 September 2027. Apply here from November 2026. Until then follow Novo Nordisk on LinkedIn to get a better feeling of who we are.
Novo Nordisk International Operations (IO) is the largest operational unit in Novo Nordisk and covers 194 countries and 95% of the world’s population. IO is split into five regions, spread across every continent of the globe. Employees working within business in Novo Nordisk have a wide range of roles and responsibilities – but all share the same commitment to excellence and to drive continued success of Novo Nordisk.
During the two-year programme you will undertake three exciting and challenging rotation of eight months each, which will include regional office/business area, affiliate and either corporate headquarters in Denmark or our International Operations office in Zurich.
You will work as a fully-fledged member of the team and build the competencies relevant to the rotation.
We are a successful global pharmaceutical company and the world leader in diabetes care. Your skills, dedication and ambition will help us continue to change lives for the better as we grow our business and help millions of people around the world.
Working at Novo Nordisk, you can therefore make a significant difference to patients and society while also delivering exciting results from a business perspective.
During the Commercial Business Graduate Programme within International Operations, you will receive training and gain knowledge and invaluable international experience leading to both professional and personal development. You will develop your core skills within areas such as project management, marketing, customer engagement or other commercial teams.
Furthermore, you will work with senior managers and build an international network of world-class colleagues, establishing yourself as one of tomorrow’s key people in business at Novo Nordisk.
We’ve designed the program so that, following its successful completion, you will be equipped with the necessary skills and experience to become a valued and promising part of our company within International Operations.
We offer a competitive entry level salary.
For the positions starting 1 September 2027, we are looking for candidates with:
A recent Master’s degree from 2026 or 2027. There may be some variations in the above requirements depending on country. You can find country specific information in the relevant job advertisement.
Relevant work experience or extracurricular activities obtained next to your studies (max one year between or after studies)
No more than 1 year of full-time work experience between or after completing a Master’s degree
Above average academic achievements
Team-player attitude, excellent communication skills, high drive and an eagerness to learn
Fluent spoken and written English
International experience, for example from studying a full semester abroad, working or volunteering
In certain hiring locations you must be legally permitted to work in that  country, please check the specific requirements in the job adverts.
You are welcome to apply for more than one track. However, we recommend you to carefully consider which tracks you will apply for and your motivation for doing so. You will have to make an individual application for each programme track and we encourage you to only apply for the tracks that you would be truly excited to join.
Be yourself and share why Novo Nordisk is the company you want to work for. What motivates you and why do you think being a graduate could be amazing. We would like to know who YOU are.
No, our corporate language is English, so speaking Danish is definitely not a requirement. There may be local language requirements for some International Operations (IO) tracks.
Yes, as long as you plan to graduate before the start of the Graduate programme. It is also accepted if you have not received your official graduate diploma before starting in the Graduate Programme, as long as you have finished your studies and are just waiting for the official papers.

Previous pharmaceutical work experience is not a requirement to apply for the programme.

Upon successful completion of the programme, you will be offered a position in Novo Nordisk, therefore full mobility and flexibility is required as the location is not pre-determined.

title: Development Academy
description:
Discover Novo Nordisk's Aseptic Manufacturing Science and Technology (AMSAT) Development Academy , a one-year programme designed to fast-track recent graduates into the world of pharmaceutical manufacturing.
Experience two rotations through various areas of our product supply operations, gaining invaluable insights into Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and emerging manufacturing processes. Your journey begins with a comprehensive onboarding month, followed by two rotations in a fun and engaging learning environment within product supply.
Upon successful completion, you will secure a guaranteed position within the company, equipped with the skills needed for a thriving career at Novo Nordisk.
Prepare for an accelerated career journey with the AMSAT Development Academy - a one-year graduate programme tailored to propel recent graduates into the fast track of professional growth.
Engage in a comprehensive learning experience , commencing with a purposeful onboarding month to set the stage for your advancement.
Forge connections and expand your network across Novo Nordisk Product Supply, AMSAT, and our global production sites, laying the foundation for a strong and supportive professional community.
Embark on a global career adventure with your first rotation in Denmark and the potential for a second rotation at an international production site , broadening your horizons and opening doors to new possibilities.
Acquire invaluable insights and practical experience in Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and emerging manufacturing processes, equipping yourself for a successful transition into your permanent position at Novo Nordisk.
Applicants should have recently completed or be on the verge of finishing a master’s degree within life science, with above average academic performance.
It is beneficial to have relevant experience in the pharmaceutical industry through studies, internships, or student jobs.
Being open to international relocation is a must, along with proficiency in spoken and written English.
Candidates should possess strong analytical skills, be able to handle diverse tasks and information effectively.
A proactive, inquisitive nature and a keenness for continuous learning are highly valued.
A collaborative mindset, great communication abilities, and the capacity to adapt swiftly are essential traits we look for.

Step 2:
Shortlisted candidates will be invited for an initial online or phone interview with the programme manager or a local HR representative. The candidates who are not invited for an interview will be notified by e-mail.

title: Development Executive - Cyber Specialty Team
description:
Company: Marsh 
 Description: 
 Job Description For Posting

 The Cyber Risk landscape continues to evolve at an accelerated rate, with continued exploitation of 0-day & Edge Devices, as well the use of deepfakes for misinformation and cyber extortion, driven by more sophisticated AI technology. It is widely recognised by Risk Managers as representing one of the most significant threats to the viability and continuity of business operations across the globe.
 
 Marsh’s global Cyber Practice is the World’s Most Trusted and Innovative Cyber Risk Advisor. Servicing clients in 130+ countries, illustrating global reach and local expertise, we pride ourselves on simplifying the complexity of Cyber. Through the application of unique Digital Tooling that is unrivalled within the marketplace, our global proprietary wordings, regional facilities, incident management support, and our global team of Cyber specialists, we provide our Clients with a holistic Cyber service proposition, helping them to Understand, Measure, Manage and Respond to Cyber Risk.  
 
 In a direct response to the increased demand and complexity of Cyber Risk, Marsh Ireland are seeking the appointment of an ambitious, motivated and results-driven Business Development Executive to join our Cyber team.  
 The individual concerned will join an existing team of motivated and enthusiastic technical Cyber specialists that are dedicated in providing Clients with Cyber Risk Service Solutions. Working closely with this team the successful candidate will benefit from comprehensive on the job training and education on Marsh Cyber solutions and services.
 
 This key role will involve maintaining responsibility and accountability for the creation and identification of new business opportunities, building and maintaining existing and prospective client relationships and working in collaboration with colleagues across the wider Marsh business to deliver our Cyber Value Proposition to new and existing clients and to drive new business revenue growth within the Cyber/Specialty practice.
 
 This represents an exciting opportunity for the right candidate with previous insurance experience ( must be CIP qualified ), ideally from a broking background, but not necessarily having significant existing Cyber and/or Financial Lines experience, and who possesses the required growth mindset, to transition themselves into a Trusted Risk and Innovated Cyber Advisor.
 With support from the wider business and the existing Team, the individual will develop strong expertise on Cyber risk, technical Cyber product knowledge and in addition will gain an in-depth understanding of and ability to articulate the Marsh Cyber Ireland Value Proposition.
 
 The role will be based in one of our ROI offices situated in Dublin or Cork or Galway and offers a hybrid working model, with 3 days in the office and 2 days remote. It will require a commitment to travel to colleague, client and prospect meetings.
 The successful candidate will be exclusively focused and dedicated to New & Expanded Cyber/Tech and FINPRO Product and Solution Sales. They will be tasked to support and implement an ambitious growth strategy and to achieve short, medium and long term growth targets.
 
 Main Activities 
 This is a sales function and the individual will be expected to develop and execute a growth strategy and development plan, aligned to our country, region and global value proposition.
 
 What can you expect: 
 To be part of an organisation with a leading global brand, a brilliant and expert team and a positive, vibrant and inclusive culture.
 You will gain the opportunity to excel and further your next career steps through intensive on the job training, interesting & challenging work, further professional development opportunities and supportive leaders.
 A key component of the role will be the Intense Technical Cyber and FINPRO training that will provide unique industry expertise.
 
 We will rely on you to:  
 Gain in-depth knowledge and understanding of Marsh’s CyberTech value proposition and develop technical working knowledge of CyberTech & FINPRO products.

 Actively seek and develop relationships with prospects and client contacts. While maintaining control and oversight of Cyber active client target/prospect list.

 Develop market profile, attend Industry Trade events/shows, compose marketing materials and insights for wider circulation on social media and Company marketing distribution.

 Draft and deliver new business presentations and support colleagues in the creation and development of expanded new business opportunities

 Identify potential growth areas, whitespace opportunities and newly developed cover solutions.

 Review Client Risk Assessments and identify potential opportunities for the provision of additional Marsh Advisory/Consulting and Incident Management services aswell as oversee, manage and coordinate the wider Cyber Advisory and Claims Incident Management services.

 Work with other business stakeholders to create increased Cross-selling opportunities. Develop and implement strategic sales plans to achieve targets and objectives.

 Conduct market research and competitor analysis to identify trends and opportunities while collaborating with marketing, product, and operations teams to align business development strategies.

 Monitor and report on sales performance metrics and suggest improvements.

 Attend industry events, conferences, and networking opportunities to promote the company and generate leads alongside staying up-to-date with industry developments and best practices.

 
 What you will need to have: 
 CIP qualification

 3 - 5 years minimum general insurance experience

 Full drivers licence and access to own car/private transportation

 Eager to learn and to enhance knowledge and technical skills

 Self-motivated and energised  

 Ability to communicate at all levels with clients & colleagues

 Team player and work with other business stakeholders

 
 What makes you stand out: 
 ACII qualification  

 Proven track record of Sales delivery is desired but not essential

 Professional certifications in sales or business development are advantageous

 
 Why join our team: 
 We help you be your best through professional development opportunities, interesting work, and supportive leaders.

 We foster a vibrant and inclusive culture where you can work with talented colleagues to create new solutions and have an impact for colleagues, clients, and communities.

 Our scale enables us to provide a range of career opportunities, as well as benefits and rewards to enhance your well-being.

 

 
 
Marsh Risk is a business of Marsh (NYSE: MRSH), a global leader in risk, reinsurance and capital, people and investments, and management consulting, advising clients in 130 countries. With annual revenue of over $27 billion and more than 95,000 colleagues, Marsh helps build the confidence to thrive through the power of perspective. For more information about Marsh Risk, visit marsh.com, or follow us on LinkedIn and X. 
 
Marsh is committed to embracing a diverse, inclusive and flexible work environment. We aim to attract and retain the best people and embrace diversity of age, background, disability, ethnic origin, family duties, gender orientation or expression, marital status, nationality, parental status, personal or social status, political affiliation, race, religion and beliefs, sex/gender, sexual orientation or expression, skin color, Traveller community, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We are an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to providing reasonable support to any candidate with a disability/health condition to allow them to fully participate in the recruitment process. We welcome candidates to contact us at reasonableaccommodations@marsh.com to discuss any specific needs. 
Marsh is committed to hybrid work, which includes the flexibility of working remotely and the collaboration, connections and professional development benefits of working together in the office. All Marsh colleagues are expected to be in their local office or working onsite with clients at least three days per week. Office-based teams will identify at least one “anchor day” per week on which their full team will be together in person.
